name: Reset_Handler
comment:
Reset_Handler, the reset entry point:
- mtcr PSR, 0xE0000200: initialize processor status
- SP = 0x2000138C: top of the 4 KB main stack
- copy 0x100 bytes vector table 0x08010400 -> 0x20000000
- copy 0x28C bytes .data 0x0807E14C -> 0x20000100
- zero .bss 0x2000038C..0x20030C78
- call SystemInit, board_init, main
- br self at 0x08010560: hang if main returns.
Literal pool at 0x08010564-0x0801058B. main is a bare-metal superloop; the FreeRTOS-style code present (vPortStartTask 0x080105E6, vTaskSwitchContext 0x0802E6B8) is never started and is dead except for the tspend IRQ path.

name: InterruptHandler
comment: InterruptHandler: common default trap handler, target of the vector-table thunk at 0x080105D0. Re-enables EE, saves the interrupted SP to g_trap_sp (0x2000158C), switches to the trap stack top 0x2000158C, builds a 0x48-byte frame with r0-r11, the interrupted SP/PC, LR, EPSR and EPC, then calls trap_c(frame). trap_c prints a register dump and spins forever, so any unexpected interrupt halts the device.

name: InterruptHandler
comment:
Alternate entry point into the trap/interrupt handler: a 2-byte unconditional branch to
InterruptHandler at 0x0801058c. The following literals hold the trap stack pointer 0x2000158c
used by the handler prologue. Kept as a separate symbol because the vector table references it.

name: cpu_yield
comment:
Yield the CPU from the current task (FreeRTOS/W806 port): writes 1 to the VIC TSPEND register
(0xE000ED04), forcing an immediate PendSV context switch. 'rts; psrclr ie' in the following bytes are
the compiler-emitted return that re-enables interrupts.

name: vPortStartTask
comment:
FreeRTOS port start: copies the first task's saved register frame from *pxCurrentTCB into
the fixed C-SKY hardware exception-save area (0x0..0xD4 and 0x40/0x400 blocks) and returns the
saved PC. The trap-return stub then resumes the task. Called once by vTaskStartScheduler.

name: tspend_handler
comment:
Context-switch trap (PendSV equivalent). Saves the interrupted C-SKY exception frame from
the fixed save area (0x0, 0x40, 0x400) to the current task's stack, stores the new stack pointer
in *pxCurrentTCB, calls vTaskSwitchContext, then copies the incoming task's saved frame back
into the hardware save area and returns its PC for the trap return.

name: sin
comment:
fdlibm double sin().
For |x| <= pi/4 it evaluates __kernel_sin directly; larger arguments go through argument
reduction (__ieee754_rem_pio2) and the quadrant selects sine or cosine kernels. Ghidra prunes
the reduction path as unreachable, so inspect the disassembly for that branch.

name: sqrt
comment:
newlib double-precision sqrt().
Handles negative/NaN/Inf/zero special cases, then computes the root with Newton-Raphson
iterations built from the soft-float helpers (__adddf3, __subdf3, __muldf3, __divdf3).

name: __kernel_poly
comment:
fdlibm polynomial evaluator (__kernel_poly): evaluates a coefficient table of degree
param_2 at x (param_3/param_4) using the soft-float multiply/add helpers. Shared by the
sine and cosine kernels.

name: __kernel_sin
comment:
fdlibm sine kernel (__kernel_sin): evaluates sin(x) for |x| <= pi/4 with the standard
13-term minimax polynomial, using __fixdfsi to split x into high and low parts.
Called by sin() after argument reduction.

name: __kernel_cos
comment:
fdlibm cosine kernel (__kernel_cos): evaluates cos(x) for |x| <= pi/4 with the standard
polynomial, using __fixdfsi to split x into high and low parts.
Called by cos() after argument reduction.

name: _rem
comment:
_rem: internal argument-reduction helper used by __ieee754_rem_pio2.
Computes fmod(x, y) and adjusts the result into [-y/2, y/2] by adding or subtracting y.
(Ghidra's prototype mangles the double arguments; y is carried in param_3/param_4.)

name: __ieee754_rem_pio2
comment:
fdlibm argument reduction (__ieee754_rem_pio2): reduces x modulo pi/2 and returns the
quadrant index plus the reduced argument as two doubles for extra precision. Uses
Cody-Waite constants for small x and the _rem Payne-Hanek path for large x.
Called by sin/cos/tan before the polynomial kernels.

name: sqrtf
comment:
sqrtf: C library wrapper that calls __ieee754_sqrtf and returns its float result.
(The decompiler mis-renders the call because __ieee754_sqrtf takes/returns floats in FP registers.)

name: __ieee754_sqrtf
comment:
fdlibm single-precision square root (__ieee754_sqrtf) used by sqrtf(): bit-level
Newton-Raphson implementation. Ghidra's decompiler prunes every block as unreachable due
to the call/return convention, so inspect the disassembly; the result is returned in r0.

name: fmod
comment:
newlib double fmod(x, y): returns x - n*y with n = truncated x/y, handling zero, Inf,
NaN and |x| < |y| special cases. Scaling steps use the soft-float helpers.
Used by floating-point formatting and user math.

name: fabs
comment:
fabs (double): clears bit 31 of the high word (r1) with bclri, returning |x|. Decompiled as
an identity due to the ABI/sret modelling of 64-bit float returns.

name: __fixunsdfsi
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert double to unsigned int (__fixunsdfsi). For negative values it
falls back to __fixdfsi; for non-negative it subtracts 2^31 (__subdf3 with 0x41E00000) before
__fixdfsi so the result fits the unsigned range.

name: __fixsfdi
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert float to signed 64-bit (__fixsfdi). Positive values go through
__fixunssfdi; negative values are converted to magnitude and negated. Argument/result are in FP
registers, which is why the decompiler shows no explicit parameter.

name: __fixdfdi
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert double to signed 64-bit (__fixdfdi). Compares with 0 (__ltdf2),
calls __fixunsdfdi for the magnitude and negates when the value is negative.

name: __fixunssfdi
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert float to unsigned 64-bit (__fixunssfdi). Extends to double,
converts the high 32-bit part with __fixunsdfsi, subtracts its double value, and converts the
remainder to produce the low 32 bits.

name: __fixunsdfdi
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert double to unsigned 64-bit (__fixunsdfdi). Splits the value:
converts the high 32-bit part with __fixunsdfsi, removes it from the double, then converts the
remainder for the low 32 bits.

name: __floatdisf
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert signed 64-bit integer to float (__floatdisf).
Rounds the low 32 bits to nearest before splitting: adds 0x1fffff (+1 if low word non-zero) and,
when rounding calls for it, clears the low 11 bits and sets bit 11 (0x800). Then computes
double(high32)*2^32 + unsigned(low32) with __floatsidf/__muldf3/__floatunsidf/__adddf3 and narrows
with __truncdfsf2.

name: __floatundidf
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert unsigned 64-bit to double (__floatundidf). Computes
double(high32)*2^32 + unsigned(low32) using __floatsidf/__muldf3/__floatunsidf/__adddf3.

name: __divdi3
comment:
Compiler runtime helper: signed 64-bit division (int64 / int64).
Leaf shift/subtract long-division loop using 32-bit register halves, with sign handling.
Called for every 64-bit division in the firmware (e.g., 64-bit sample timing math).

name: __moddi3
comment:
Compiler runtime helper: signed 64-bit remainder (int64 % int64).
Result takes the sign of the dividend; leaf shift/subtract implementation.

name: __udivdi3
comment:
Compiler runtime helper: unsigned 64-bit division (uint64 / uint64).
Leaf shift/subtract long-division loop over 32-bit register halves.

name: __umoddi3
comment:
Compiler runtime helper: unsigned 64-bit remainder (uint64 % uint64).
Leaf shift/subtract implementation.

name: __extendsfdf2
comment:
Soft-float helper: extend float to double (__extendsfdf2). Unpacks the float, shifts the
24-bit mantissa into the 53-bit double mantissa (<<30, >>2 split) and builds the double with
__make_dp. W806 has no FPU, so this is used for every float-to-double conversion.

name: _fpadd_parts
comment:
Core routine of the newlib soft-float add/sub implementation.
Takes two unpacked double values (param_1, param_2), handles NaN/Inf/zero/denormal
special cases, aligns exponents and adds/subtracts the mantissas into param_3.
Called by __adddf3 and __subdf3.

name: __adddf3
comment:
Soft-float helper: double addition (__adddf3). Unpacks both operands, adds with
_fpadd_parts, and repacks the newlib _fp_double structure with __pack_d.

name: __subdf3
comment:
Soft-float helper: double subtraction (__subdf3). Flips the sign bit of the second
unpacked operand (_fp_double sign ^= 1) and adds via _fpadd_parts, then packs.

name: __muldf3
comment:
Soft-float double-precision multiply (__muldf3).
Unpacks both operands with __unpack_d, multiplies the 32-bit mantissa halves using
__muldi3, normalizes/rounds and packs the result with __pack_d. All double arithmetic in
the firmware goes through these helpers because the W806 has no FPU.

name: __divdf3
comment:
Soft-float double-precision divide (__divdf3).
Unpacks operands with __unpack_d, performs restoring division of the mantissas, normalizes/
rounds and packs the result with __pack_d.

name: __nedf2
comment:
Soft-float comparison: != for doubles (__nedf2). Unpacks both operands and returns
__fpcmp_parts_d's result (non-zero when unequal); NaN inputs are treated as unequal.

name: __gtdf2
comment:
Soft-float comparison: > for doubles (__gtdf2). Returns __fpcmp_parts_d, or -1 when
either operand is NaN/unordered (C semantics: comparison false).

name: __gedf2
comment:
Soft-float comparison: >= for doubles (__gedf2). Returns __fpcmp_parts_d, or -1 when
either operand is NaN/unordered.

name: __ltdf2
comment:
Soft-float comparison: < for doubles (__ltdf2). Returns __fpcmp_parts_d's result,
treating NaN/unordered comparisons as false.

name: __floatsidf
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert signed int to double (__floatsidf).
Normalizes |value| with LZCOUNT, builds a newlib _fp_double struct (class 3 = normal, sign, exponent
0x3c-lz, normalized mantissa) and packs it with __pack_d. Zero uses class 2. Custom LZCOUNT inline,
not a stock newlib build.

name: __fixdfsi
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert double to signed int (__fixdfsi).
Unpacks the double, returns 0 for values below 1.0, saturates to 0x7fffffff (or 0x80000000 for
negative) for large/inf/nan, otherwise shifts the 64-bit mantissa right by the exponent and applies
the sign. No FPU on W806, so all doubles go through these newlib routines.

name: __make_dp
comment:
Soft-float internals: build a double from the fields of a newlib _fp_double (class,
sign, exponent, mantissa, extra) and pack it via __pack_d. Used by __extendsfdf2.

name: __truncdfsf2
comment:
Soft-float helper: truncate double to float (__truncdfsf2). Unpacks the double, builds the
24-bit float mantissa (<<2 plus upper bits of the extra word, sticky OR when lower bits are
lost) and packs with __make_fp.

name: __floatunsidf
comment:
Soft-float helper: convert unsigned int to double (__floatunsidf). Zero becomes class 2;
otherwise normalizes with LZCOUNT and builds the _fp_double fields before __pack_d.

name: __muldi3
comment:
64-bit integer multiply (__muldi3): operands in r0:r1 and r2:r3, 64-bit product returned
in r0:r1. Uses 16-bit partial products with carry propagation. Ghidra decompiles only the low
word because the high half is returned in r1 through the ABI.

name: __unpack_f
comment:
newlib soft-float helper __unpack_f: splits an IEEE-754 float into sign, unbiased exponent
and 24-bit mantissa and classifies zero/denormal/Inf/NaN.

name: __make_fp
__pack_d
comment:
newlib soft-float helper __pack_d: packs an unpacked double (sign, exponent, 56-bit
mantissa) back into IEEE-754 format with round-to-nearest-even, handling overflow,
underflow, denormals, Inf and NaN.

name: __unpack_d
comment:
newlib soft-float helper __unpack_d: splits an IEEE-754 double into sign, unbiased
exponent and 56-bit mantissa and classifies zero/denormal/Inf/NaN for the arithmetic
routines.

name: __fpcmp_parts_d
comment:
newlib soft-float comparison of two unpacked doubles (__fpcmp_parts_d).
Handles NaN, Inf and zero classes, then compares signs, exponents and mantissas. Used by
the __eqdf2/__nedf2/__ltdf2/__gtdf2/__ledf2/__gedf2 helpers.

name: __pack_f
comment:
newlib soft-float helper __pack_f: packs an unpacked single-precision float back into
IEEE-754 with rounding and denormal/overflow handling.

name: putchar
comment:
putchar: forward the character to putc() on stdout (FILE* from the C library). Used by printf
when char output is enabled; _out_uart is the actual UART backend.

name: puts
comment:
puts: write the string plus a newline to stdout via fputs/fputc (C library). Used for the
upgrade/boot status messages on the debug UART.

name: fputs
comment: newlib fputs: writes the C string character by character through fputc inside the os_critical enter/exit hooks, stopping at the NUL terminator. Returns the number of characters written, or -1 when the stream or string pointer is NULL.

name: rand
comment:
rand: 32-bit LCG (state = state*0x41C64E6D + 0x3039) returning state>>1. State lives at
0x200001b8; seed it with srand.

name: srand
comment: srand: seed the C library PRNG by storing the seed in the 32-bit rand_state global.

name: memset
comment:
Standard C memset: fills __n bytes at __s with __c, aligning to a 4-byte boundary and then
writing 16-byte blocks of a replicated 32-bit pattern for speed, with a byte tail.

name: memcpy
comment:
Standard C memcpy: copies __n bytes from __src to __dest. For word-aligned buffers it uses
16-byte blocks and 4-byte words, then a byte tail; unaligned buffers use a byte copy.

name: os_critical_open
comment: OS critical-section open hook: stub returning 0 (W806 port does not implement it).

name: os_critical_enter
comment:
OS critical-section enter hook: stub returning 0. Real masking is done elsewhere (see the
interrupt enable/disable helpers); this symbol satisfies the OS adaptation layer.

name: os_critical_exit
comment: OS critical-section exit hook: stub returning 0.

name: os_critical_close
comment: OS critical-section close hook: stub returning 0.

name: putc
comment:
putc: newlib stdio entry that forwards to fputc for the given stream (the W806 build
implements character output directly over UART0).

name: HAL_GPIO_Init
comment: HAL GPIO initialization: walks the Pin mask in GPIO_InitTypeDef and programs direction, AF select/mux registers, pull-up/pull-down, interrupt mode and input-buffer enable in the W806 GPIO block. Called from zw_gpio_init_hw.

name: HAL_GPIO_DeInit
comment:
De-initialize GPIO pin(s): for each bit set in GPIO_Pin, clears the direction bit, enables
the pull-up, disables pull-down, clears input-mode/source/edge selections and disables the pin
interrupt. Leaves the pin as a pulled-up input in the reset-like state.

name: HAL_UART_Init
comment:
HAL UART initialization.
Calls HAL_UART_MspInit when the handle is not yet initialized, programs the line control
register (word length, parity, stop bits from Init), FIFO thresholds, enables TX/RX, and
computes the baud-rate divisor from the APB clock (integer part in baud register, fractional
part in bits 16+). Returns 0 on success, 1 for a null handle.

name: HAL_UART_DeInit
comment:
De-initialize a UART: if huart is non-NULL, clears the LC register clock/enable bits,
calls HAL_UART_MspDeInit (pins/clocks/IRQ), resets the transfer counters and state, and returns
HAL_OK; NULL returns HAL_ERROR.

name: HAL_UART_Transmit
comment:
HAL_UART_Transmit: blocking transmit of pData/Size bytes.
Returns HAL_BUSY if the handle is busy, HAL_ERROR on null/zero arguments, otherwise waits
for TX FIFO space (FIFOS & 0x3f < 0x20), writes bytes to TDW, and polls the FIFO empty at
the end. Timeout is measured with HAL_GetTick (0xffffffff = wait forever); on expiry the
handle is left idle and HAL_TIMEOUT is returned.

name: HAL_UART_Receive_IT
HAL_UART_TxCpltCallback
comment: HAL UART transmit-complete weak callback: empty default implementation (no action).

name: HAL_UART_IRQHandler
comment:
UART interrupt handler (WM HAL).
Clears the interrupt status, then: on RX FIFO threshold/timeout reads bytes from RDW into
huart->pRxBuffPtr, tracks RxXferCount and calls HAL_UART_RxCpltCallback when full; on TXE
writes words from pTxBuffPtr to TDW while the FIFO has room; on TX complete disables the
TX interrupt and calls HAL_UART_TxCpltCallback. UART4 has a special short-FIFO drain path.

name: SystemClock_Get
comment: Derive CPU/AHB/APB and peripheral clock frequencies from the PLL and divider fields of system register 0x40000E10. The decompiler shows truncated uRam00000e00 addresses; disassembly confirms 0x40000E10.

name: HAL_InitTick
comment:
Initialize the 1 ms HAL time base: programs the core timer (CORET) reload from the APB
clock (0x1e0/divider * 1e6/1000 - 1), enables it (CSR=7), clears VIC pending/enable for the
core timer IRQ and stores the tick priority. Called from HAL_Init.

name: SystemClock_Config
comment: Configure the W806 clock tree: writes 0x40000E00, 0x40000E08 = 0xF and the PLL/pre-divider fields in 0x40000E10, then starts the HAL tick via HAL_InitTick(7). The decompiler misrenders these as uRam00000e00 etc.; disassembly confirms 0x40000E00/08/10.

name: HAL_IncTick
comment: HAL_IncTick: increment the 1 ms system tick counter. Called from the SysTick handler.

name: HAL_GetTick
comment: HAL_GetTick: return the 1 ms tick counter (uwTick), incremented by HAL_IncTick from SysTick.

name: HAL_NVIC_SetPriority
comment:
Set an interrupt priority: writes the 2-bit priority into the VIC priority register byte
at 0xE000E400 (base+0x300) for IRQn, clearing the 8-bit field first. IRQn with the SEC bit
set addresses the secure bank (byte shift by 8).

name: HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ
comment:
Enable an NVIC/VIC interrupt: writes 1<<(IRQn&31) to the VIC ISER bank (0xE000E100/104)
and mirrors the same bit to the register at ISER+0x140, used by the W806 VIC to latch the
enable/pending state.

name: HAL_NVIC_DisableIRQ
comment:
Disable an NVIC/VIC interrupt: writes 1<<(IRQn&31) to the VIC ICER bank
(ISER0 0xE000E100 + (bank+0x20)*4, i.e. 0xE000E180/0xE000E184).

name: SPI_Receive_IT
comment:
SPI RX interrupt service helper: reads the RX FIFO level from STATUS bits 8-10 and moves
up to four bytes per 32-bit RXDATA word into hspi->pRxBuffPtr, decrementing RxXferCount until
the requested length or the FIFO is drained.

name: HAL_SPI_Init
comment:
Initialize the SPI controller: on reset takes the lock and calls HAL_SPI_MspInit, then
programs CH_CFG (NSS, master enable), SPI_CFG (mode, clock polarity/phase, first bit), CLK_CFG
(prescaler) from hspi->Init, enables the SPI (CH_CFG |= 4) and marks the handle READY.

name: HAL_SPI_Transmit
comment: Blocking SPI transmit in chunks of up to 0x1FF8 bytes: locks the handle, selects TX mode, fills the W806 SPI FIFO, waits for completion or timeout and returns HAL status. Used by the FPGA register and sample-transfer helpers.

name: HAL_SPI_Receive
comment: Blocking SPI receive in chunks of up to 0x1FF8 bytes: locks the handle, selects RX mode, drains the W806 SPI FIFO into the caller buffer, waits for completion or timeout and returns HAL status. Used by the FPGA register and sample-transfer helpers.

name: HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback
comment: HAL SPI Tx-complete weak callback: empty default implementation (no action).

name: HAL_SPI_RxCpltCallback
comment: HAL SPI Rx-complete weak callback: empty default implementation (no action).

name: HAL_SPI_TxRxCpltCallback
comment: HAL SPI Tx/Rx-complete weak callback: empty default implementation (no action).

name: HAL_SPI_IRQHandler
comment: SPI interrupt handler for the low-speed SPI block (vector 44). Decodes the SPI status flags, services TX/RX/DMA completion and error conditions, invokes HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback / RxCpltCallback / TxRxCpltCallback, and starts the next DMA transfer when needed.

name: HAL_WDG_DeInit
comment:
De-initialize the watchdog: disable the WDG interrupt, clear the control register and write
1 to CLR to reset the counter. Used before long flash upgrades.

name: HAL_WDG_MspInit
comment: HAL watchdog MSP init hook: empty (the WDG needs no pin/clock setup on this SoC).

name: HAL_WDG_Init
comment:
Initialize the watchdog: runs the MSP hook, computes the reload value as
Init.Reload * APB clock from SystemClock_Get and writes LD, then enables the watchdog (CR=3).

name: __readByCMD
comment:
Low-level flash read through the W806 flash controller.
Programs the read command and address into flash_ctrl_cmd_info/flash_ctrl_addr, starts the
operation by writing 0x100 to flash_ctrl_cmd_start, then copies the requested words via the
flash read cache at PTR_flashRead_cache and fixes up unaligned leading bytes. (Ghidra loses
the flash base register in the copy loop, so the source renders as address 0.)

name: flashRead
comment:
Low-level serial-flash read with 256-byte cache at 0x20001590 (flashRead_cache).
Reads an arbitrary address/length through the flash controller's read command, refilling
one 256-byte page at a time. Backs settings, calibration and screenshot access.

name: HAL_FLASH_Read
comment: Reads SPI flash into buf. 'addr' is relative to flash base 0x08000000. Only called by HAL_FLASH_Read_Offset_0x96000.

name: HAL_FLASH_Write
comment: Writes a buffer to SPI flash. 'addr' is relative to flash base 0x08000000. Performs a read-modify-write per 4KB page: flashRead() the page into cache, merge 'len' bytes, erase the page, then program in 0x100-byte chunks. Only called by HAL_FLASH_Write_Offset_0x96000.

name: zw_flash_read_uuid
comment:
Reads the 18-byte flash-chip signature (manufacturer/length/device ID) with flash
controller command 0x2C09F. main() compares it with the factory record at 0x08096000
and halts on mismatch (yellow screen) to detect a different flash chip/board.

name: HAL_ADC_Start
comment:
Start an ADC conversion: writes the channel selection into ANA_CR, clears both interrupt
flags (IF=3), then sets the channel plus enable bits (3) in ANA_CR and unlocks the handle.

name: HAL_ADC_Init
comment:
HAL ADC initialization.
Enables the ADC clock, programs the ADC clock divider from the APB clock and Init.freq,
configures the PGA (gain 3) and analog bias registers, then calibrates by polling four
conversions and loading the trim value from the chip information block at 0x200 into the
offset field before leaving the ADC enabled.

name: HAL_ADC_GET_INPUT_VOLTAGE
comment:
HAL_ADC_GET_INPUT_VOLTAGE: performs 4 ADC conversions (starting the ADC if needed),
restores the analog block and converts the trim-corrected raw value
((info-block 0x200 value) - hadc->offset) to a voltage in millivolts using double scaling
and __fixdfsi. Used by the battery monitor.

name: HAL_ADC_ConvCpltCallback
comment: HAL ADC conversion-complete weak callback: empty default implementation (no action).

name: HAL_ADC_CompareCallback
comment: HAL ADC analog-watchdog compare weak callback: empty default implementation (no action).

name: HAL_ADC_IRQHandler
comment:
ADC interrupt service: if the conversion-complete interrupt is enabled and flag 1 is set,
clears it and calls HAL_ADC_ConvCpltCallback; if the analog-watchdog interrupt is enabled and
flag 2 is set, clears it and calls HAL_ADC_CompareCallback.

name: __PWM_OutMode_Config
comment:
Configures a PWM channel output mode (OutMode):
0 = output disabled (clears complementary and channel enable bits),
1 = channel output enabled (sets CR bit channel/2+0xe),
2 = complementary/PWM output with dead time (programs DTCR for channel 0/2),
3 = force output low (CR bit 6),
4 = set brake bit for the channel. Returns HAL_OK.

name: __PWM_CountType_Config
comment:
PWM counter-mode configuration: channels 0-3 write CounterMode into CR bits
[(Channel+8)*2, +8); channel 4 writes bits [5:3] of CH4CR2 (up/down/center-aligned mode).

name: __PWM_Freq_Config
comment:
__PWM_Freq_Config: sets the prescaler and period for a PWM channel
(hpwm->Channel 0..4) by writing CLKDIV01/CLKDIV23/PERIOD or CH4CR1, preserving the fields
belonging to the other channels. Returns HAL_OK.

name: __PWM_Duty_Config
comment:
Program an 8-bit PWM compare (duty) value for a channel.
Channel 0 -> CMPDAT[7:0], 1 -> CMPDAT[15:8], 2 -> CMPDAT[31:16], 3 -> CMPDAT[31:24]
(mask 0x7fffff first) and channel 4 -> CH4CR2[15:8]. All other channel numbers are ignored.
Always returns HAL_OK.

name: __PWM_AutoReload_Config
comment:
PWM auto-reload preload configuration: channels 0-3 set CR bit (Channel+8); channel 4
sets bit 1 of CH4CR2. Enables buffering of the auto-reload register on the next update.

name: __PWM_OutInverse_Config
comment:
PWM output-inverse configuration: channels 0-3 set CR bit (Channel+2); channel 4 sets
bit 0 of CH4CR2. Inverts the corresponding PWM output polarity.

name: HAL_PWM_Init
HAL_PWM_Start
comment:
Start a PWM channel: if hpwm is non-NULL, sets bit (27+Channel) in the PWM instance
control register (offset +8) and returns HAL_OK; NULL returns HAL_ERROR.

name: HAL_PWM_Stop
comment:
Stop a PWM channel: if hpwm is non-NULL, clears bit (27+Channel) in the PWM instance
control register (offset +8) and returns HAL_OK; NULL returns HAL_ERROR.

name: HAL_PWM_Duty_Set
comment:
HAL PWM duty-cycle setter: if hpwm is NULL returns HAL_ERROR; otherwise forwards
(hpwm, Channel, Pulse) unchanged to __PWM_Duty_Config and returns HAL_OK. Kept as a thin HAL
wrapper so callers (backlight, siggen, DMM bias) share the same null check.

name: DMA_SetConfig
comment:
Programs a DMA channel for a transfer: clears the channel's interrupt flags, then
according to Init.Mode writes source/destination/word-length registers for normal mode
(0), linked-descriptor double-buffer mode (split length into two descriptors, mode != 1)
or auto-reload/ring mode (1, sets SA/DA/SWA/DWA/WLEN with source/destination wrap).

name: HAL_DMA_Init
comment:
HAL DMA initialization.
Derives the channel index from the instance address, resets CR2/MODE, programs the transfer
direction, request source (including the UART request select register) and data
alignment/increment fields; modes 2/3 build a two-entry linked-descriptor ring for
double-buffered transfers. Sets the handle to READY/UNLOCKED and returns HAL_OK.

name: HAL_DMA_Start_IT
comment:
Start a DMA transfer in interrupt mode (HAL layer).
Rejects if the handle is locked or not READY (returns HAL_BUSY). Marks the channel BUSY, clears the
error code, disables the channel (CR1 bit1 set, wait until enable bit0 clears), programs source/
destination/length via DMA_SetConfig, unmasks the channel's completion interrupt in the global IM
register (IM &= ~(2 << (ChannelIndex*2))) and enables the channel (CR1 bit0).

name: HAL_DMA_IRQHandler
comment:
HAL DMA interrupt handler.
Handles the channel's transfer-complete flag: normal mode clears/sets the mask and calls
XferCpltCallback; ring mode (1) advances the current address in CR2 and wraps it at 0xffff
via the CR1 disable/enable sequence; linked-descriptor modes (2/3) alternate half/full
callbacks between the two descriptors. The channel flag is cleared at the end.

name: HAL_WDG_Init_wrapper
comment:
Re-initialize the watchdog after an upgrade/exit path: points the global hwdg handle at the
WDG register block, restores its prescaler/config word and calls HAL_WDG_Init.

name: zw_main
comment: Application entry: hardware bring-up, UI/scope/DMM/siggen initialization, then the bare-metal main superloop.

name: fls_drv_read_id
comment:
Flash driver 'read ID' stub: returns the caller's pointer unchanged, i.e. leaves the ID buffer
untouched. The W806 internal flash ID is not read through this path.

name: HAL_ADC_MspInit
comment:
ADC MSP initialization (only for ADC instance 0x200).
Enables the ADC/analog clocks (bits 0x1800 in 0x40000E00) and configures the GPIOA pin mux
for the selected channel: 0=PA1, 0x100=PA4, 0x200=PA3, 0x300=PA2, 0x800=PA1+PA4,
0x900=PA3+PA2, setting the analog/input mode bits for each pin.

name: HAL_PWM_MspInit
comment:
PWM MSP init: enables the PWM clock (0x40000E00 |= 0x2000) and configures the PWM pins
PA2 (mask 4) and PA3 (mask 8) with their alternate-function select/input-enable bits, plus PB25
(mask 0x2000000, the signal-generator output).

name: HAL_UART_MspInit
comment:
UART MSP initialization: enables the peripheral clocks (writes 0x40000E00) and sets the
GPIO pin mux for each UART instance. UART3 (0x40010C00) uses GPIOB PB0/PB1 (clock bit
0x810), UART4 uses GPIOA PA8/PA9 (0x820), and the third instance (0x1000) uses GPIOA PA13
(0x840). All enable the shared UART2_5 IRQ at priority 0.

name: HAL_UART_MspDeInit
comment:
UART MSP de-init: matches huart->Instance and releases the corresponding pins and clock
gate: UART3 (0x40010C00) -> PB0/PB1 + clock bit 0x10, UART4 (0x40010E00) -> PA8/PA9 + bit 0x20,
voice UART (instance 0x1000) -> PA13 + bit 0x40. Pins are left pulled-up via HAL_GPIO_DeInit.

name: HAL_SPI_MspInit
comment:
SPI MSP initialization: enables the GPIO clocks and configures the low-speed SPI signals
(GPIOA pin 0 and GPIOB pins 16/17/24), sets up the TX and RX DMA channels
(hdma_spi_tx/hdma_spi_rx, structs with channel/priority fields, then HAL_DMA_Init), and
enables the SPI_LS interrupt at priority 1.

name: CORET_IRQHandler
comment:
Core-timer (SysTick) vector. Saves the C-SKY exception save area (0x48 block and
0x41c/0x400 block) on the stack, calls HAL_IncTick for the 1 ms time base, then restores the
context and returns. The save/restore sequences are the SDK's fixed-address interrupt frame.

name: ADC_IRQHandler
comment:
ADC interrupt vector: saves the fixed C-SKY exception frame, calls
HAL_ADC_IRQHandler(hadc) for the global ADC handle, then restores the frame.

name: UART1_IRQHandler
comment:
Shared UART2_5/voice interrupt vector: saves the fixed C-SKY exception frame, dispatches
HAL_UART_IRQHandler for the FPGA UART3, the DMM UART4 and the voice-module UART (instance 0x1000),
then restores the frame.

name: HAL_UART_RxCpltCallback
comment:
UART receive-complete callback.
For UART3 it calls zw_uart_rx_interrupt_handler_logic (FPGA upgrade protocol parser); for
UART4 it copies the 10-byte DMM frame into dmm_rx_buffer; for the instance at 0x1000 it
copies a 10-byte frame into a second buffer.

name: SPI_LS_IRQHandler
comment:
SPI interrupt vector: saves the fixed C-SKY exception frame, calls HAL_SPI_IRQHandler for
the shared ST7789/FPGA SPI handle, then restores the frame.

name: DMA_Channel0_IRQHandler
comment:
DMA channel 0 interrupt vector: saves the fixed C-SKY exception frame, calls
HAL_DMA_IRQHandler for the SPI TX DMA handle, then restores the frame.

name: DMA_Channel1_IRQHandler
comment:
DMA channel 1 interrupt vector: saves the fixed C-SKY exception frame, calls
HAL_DMA_IRQHandler for the SPI RX DMA handle, then restores the frame.

name: zw_calib_step_ch1_gain
comment: Calibration step for the CH1 gain/ADC reference: averages the 300-sample trace pairs over several iterations, compares the result against the 0x7F/0x80 target, steps the CH1 sensitivity index settings[0x42] and adjusts the AFE offset through zw_scope_ch1_update_afe_offset until centered. Returns 0 while waiting, 1 to continue, 2 when finished. Called by zw_auto_calibration_handler.

name: zw_calib_step_ch1_offset
comment:
Guided calibration step: CH1 DC offset.
Waits until the input is stable (max-min < 0x33) and the step counter reaches 5, averages
600 samples from the two 300-sample buffers, then adjusts the CH1 offset calibration byte
for the current range (index settings[0x42]+0x70) so the average approaches 0x7f. Advances
through ranges 4..13 and refreshes hardware; returns 1 while more ranges remain, 2 when the
sequence is complete.

name: zw_calib_step_ch2_gain
comment: Calibration step for the CH2 gain/ADC reference: averages 300-sample trace pairs over five passes, compares against the 0x7F/0x80 target, trims the CH2 calibration entry indexed by settings[0x80] and adjusts the AFE offset through zw_scope_ch2_update_afe_offset. Returns 0 waiting, 1 continue, 2 finished. Called by zw_auto_calibration_handler.

name: zw_calib_step_ch1_adc_reference
comment:
Guided calibration step: CH1 ADC reference (high).
Accumulates 300x2 samples over 25 steps, converts the average to the ADC reference value
and stores 75000/(avg-0x7f) at calibration buffer +0x80 when the average is in 0xc1..0xd3
(otherwise 1000). Returns 1 when the measurement is complete.

name: zw_calib_step_ch1_adc_reference_low
comment:
Guided calibration step: CH1 ADC reference (low).
Accumulates 300x2 samples over 25 steps and stores 75000/(0x7f-avg) at calibration buffer
+0x88 when the average is in 0x2b..0x3d (otherwise 1000). Returns 1 when complete.

name: zw_calib_step_ch2_adc_reference
comment:
Guided calibration step: CH2 ADC reference (high).
Same algorithm as the CH1 variant but stores the result at calibration buffer +0x84.
Returns 1 when the 25-step measurement is complete.

name: zw_calib_step_ch2_adc_reference_low
comment:
Guided calibration step: CH2 ADC reference (low).
Same algorithm as the CH1 low-reference step but stores the result at calibration buffer
+0x8c. Returns 1 when complete.

name: zw_save_calibration_to_flash
comment: Writes the 0x8E-byte scope/AFE calibration record to flash offset 0x2000 + 0x96000 = absolute 0x08098000.

name: zw_auto_calibration_handler
comment: Auto-calibration runner (settings[1]==5), called from main. Backs up the 0x154-byte settings block, resets calibration defaults, shows CALIB, then executes ten states (CH1/CH2 offset and gain, ADC reference high/low, preparation and save) through the state table; persists results with zw_save_calibration_to_flash and restores the backup, reporting DONE or FAILED on timeout.

name: zw_load_calibration
comment:
Loads scope calibration (0x8E bytes at flash +0x2000) and DMM calibration (0x30 bytes
at +0x2400). Invalid scope data falls back to 990000 gain / 1000 marker defaults; each
DMM calibration value outside 4000..6500 is replaced by 5000. Results go to
scope_calib_buffer and dmm_calib_buffer.

name: zw_calibration_menu_handler
comment:
Calibration mode 1 handler (settings[0x12a]==1).
Keys 0x21/0x23 increment and 0x22/0x24 decrement the value settings+0x70; keys 3/4 adjust
settings+0xb0. Key 2 runs the frequency-meter reference calibration when enabled, saves
settings to flash (offset 0x1000) and shows 'OK'; key 1 exits; key 0x14 restores both
values to 1000 and saves.

name: zw_calibration_fine_tune_handler
comment:
Calibration mode 2 handler (settings[0x12a]==2).
Applies +/-200 fine tuning to all 14 CH1 calibration entries (keys 0x21/0x23 add,
0x22/0x24 subtract) or all 14 CH2 entries (keys 3/4), then updates the CH1/CH2 AFE
offsets. Key 2 saves the calibration to flash with an 'OK' popup, key 1 exits.

name: zw_calibration_per_range_handler
comment:
Calibration mode 3 handler (settings[0x12a]==3).
Keys 0x21/0x23 add 200 and 0x22/0x24 subtract 200 to/from the current range's entry in the
scope calibration buffer (index settings[0x42]); keys 3/4 adjust entry settings[0x80]+0xe.
Every change re-applies the CH1/CH2 AFE offsets; key 2 saves the calibration to flash with
an 'OK' popup and key 1 exits.

name: zw_cursor_init
comment:
Initializes the cursor UI descriptors and defaults: three cursor elements (positions,
colors, visibility) and the cursor info box, plus the default cursor x positions at
settings+0x100..0x106 (-105, 105, 85, -85) and settings+0x142 = 85.

name: zw_cursor_movement_handler
comment: Moves the measurement cursors within the plot bounds while cursor mode is active (settings[0xFC] nonzero): events 0x2B/0x2C move cursor A horizontally, 0x30/0x31 cursor B, and the remaining events move the voltage cursors, clamping each to +-0x94 px (x) and the plot height (y). Called from main.

name: zw_scope_cursor_measurements_window
comment: Draws the cursor measurement box and dashed cursor lines. Cursor mode comes from settings[0xFC], the A/B x positions from settings +0x100/+0x102; the routine computes the delta time/frequency and delta voltage using the timebase and vertical scale, draws the two dashed vertical lines over the plot and renders the numeric readouts. Called from zw_scope_ui_refresh.

name: zw_fpga_all_reset
comment:
Reset the FPGA logic array: sends the FPGA SPI command byte 1 (soft reset). Called during
power-up and after a failed acquisition to return the FPGA to a known state.

name: zw_fpga_acq_stop
comment: Stop the FPGA acquisition engine: sends SPI command 1 with parameter 2 (stop/abort current capture).

name: zw_fpga_set_mode_reg
comment: Rebuild FPGA config register 2 from global_settings (channel/run mode in settings[2], bit 2 from settings[0xDD] roll flag, bit 6 from settings[0x147]) while preserving bits 3-5 and 7, then write it.

name: zw_fpga_set_highspeed_flag
comment:
Set the FPGA high-speed mode flag: updates bit 7 of the cached FPGA config word at
0x2000289c and sends the word with FPGA SPI register 2.

name: zw_fpga_acq_reset
comment: Pulse the FPGA acquisition reset by writing 2 then 4 to config register 1.

name: zw_fpga_set_adc_interleave
comment:
Set the FPGA dual-ADC interleave mode: updates bit 4 of the cached FPGA config word at
0x2000289c, writes it to FPGA SPI register 2, then sends command 1/parameter 8 to apply the ADC
phase configuration.

name: zw_fpga_set_pwm_val
comment:
Set the FPGA's internal PWM/voltage value: writes register 0x1a over the FPGA SPI link
(used for DAC/PWM-style analog controls inside the FPGA).

name: zw_system_power_control
comment:
Master power control for the acquisition hardware: sets/clears bit 0 of the cached FPGA
config byte, sends it to the FPGA as SPI command 6, and starts/stops the system-power PWM
(hpwm1) via zw_HAL_PWM_Start/Stop_wrapper. param != 0 = power on.

name: zw_power_on
comment:
Power-on handling: if settings[0xf9] enables it, switches the system power on
(zw_system_power_control(1)), sets the power-state flag at 0x200028a4 and arms the off timer
for param_1 seconds (milliseconds*1000 us).

name: zw_auto_power_off_check
comment: If the auto-power-off flag is set and its idle timer expires, call zw_system_power_control(0) to switch the instrument off and clear the flag.

name: zw_fpga_counter_reset
comment: Reset the FPGA sample counter: SPI command 1, parameter 0x100.

name: zw_fpga_set_counter_gate
comment:
Set the FPGA counter gate: updates bit 16 of the cached FPGA control word at 0x200028a0
from param_1, then writes the full word to FPGA SPI register 0x17 (gates/starts the sample
counter used for time-base measurements).

name: zw_fpga_read_counter
comment:
Read the FPGA's internal sample counter: issues the FPGA SPI register read for register 0x18
and returns the value from zw_fpga_spi_read_reg.

name: zw_fpga_counter_disable_and_clear
comment:
Disable and clear the FPGA sample counter: clears bit 16 of the cached control word at
0x200028a0, writes it to FPGA SPI register 0x17, then sends command 1/parameter 0x200 to clear
the counter value.

name: zw_calculate_frequency
comment: Reads the FPGA frequency counter (registers 0x18/0x19 plus flag register 0x0F) and converts the counter and time-base values into period and frequency. Returns 0 on counter overflow, 2 when no signal/timeout is detected, and returns the 64-bit result through param_1. Called by zw_scope_frequency_meter.

name: zw_fpga_set_freq_meter_triggers
comment:
Program the FPGA frequency-meter trigger configuration: builds the cached register-0x17
word as param_2 | (param_1 << 8) and sends it over FPGA SPI. Used by the frequency counter to
select trigger source/edges.

name: zw_siggen_freq_duty
comment:
Program signal-generator frequency and duty. Converts freq into the FPGA DDS phase
increment using 64-bit scaling (freq<<28 divided by freq>>4 with a constant divisor, rounding
up at small remainders) and writes it to FPGA SPI register 0x10; scales duty to per-mille
(duty<<28 / (duty>>4) / 1000) and writes it to register 0x11. Diagnostic printf is compiled out.

name: zw_fpga_load_siggen_wave_buffer
comment:
Upload a 256-entry (512-byte) 16-bit waveform table to the signal generator: sets bit 2
of the cached FPGA config byte, sends SPI command 6, writes each halfword through FPGA SPI
register 0x10 (auto-incrementing), restores the previous streaming bit state, sends command 6
again, and finally reprograms frequency/duty from settings+0xf0 and settings+0xec.

name: zw_siggen_enable_control
comment:
Enable/disable the signal-generator output. Enable: sets bit 1 of the cached FPGA config
byte and sends SPI command 6. Disable: zero-fills a 1 KB buffer, uploads it as the wave table
(zw_fpga_load_siggen_wave_buffer), clears bit 1 and sends command 6, silencing the output.

name: zw_fpga_set_sample_rate
comment: Compute the FPGA sample-rate divider from the timebase in global_settings (+0xC0/+0xC4) and write config register 7. Encoding depends on settings[2] (1-channel vs 2-channel mode) and has special cases for dividers 1/2/5/25 and even-divider flags 0x400000/0x8400000.

name: zw_fpga_set_trigger_config
comment: Build and write FPGA config register 5: the trigger level from settings +0x40 clamped to 8..250 plus the +-10 hysteresis window, with settings[0x38] in bit 16 and settings[0x3A] in bit 17.

name: zw_fpga_set_pre_trigger
comment: Write FPGA config register 0xE with the pre-trigger sample count from settings +0xC8 (biased by 0x400), doubled in 2-channel mode.

name: zw_fpga_set_post_trigger
comment: Write FPGA config register 8 with the post-trigger sample count from settings +0xCC (biased by 0x400), doubled in 2-channel mode.

name: zw_fpga_update_all_configs
comment: Push the whole acquisition configuration to the FPGA: mode register, sample rate, trigger configuration, pre/post-trigger counts and acquisition reset. Called after settings changes.

name: zw_fpga_set_acq_mode_continuous
comment: Put the FPGA acquisition engine in continuous (run) mode: SPI command 1, parameter 0x80.

name: zw_fpga_set_acq_mode_single
comment: Put the FPGA acquisition engine in single-shot mode: SPI command 1, parameter 0x40.

name: zw_fpga_read_trigger_addr
comment:
Read the FPGA trigger address: reads SPI register 9 (trigger position in the sample
buffer). In non-roll mode (settings[0xdd]==0) subtracts 4 and wraps by adding the buffer length
when negative; when dual-ADC/interleave mode is active (settings[2]==1) divides by 2 to convert
the byte address into a sample-pair index.

name: zw_fpga_read_adc_values
comment:
Read both FPGA-internal ADC values: SPI register read 0x12, then split the word into
high byte (*param_1) and low byte (*param_2). Used by the dual-ADC interleave check.

name: zw_fpga_read_status
comment:
Read the FPGA status word: SPI register read 0x14, result stored at *param_1. The status bits
are decoded by the zw_fpga_check_* helpers and the acquisition state machine.

name: zw_fpga_set_data_read_params
comment:
Programs the FPGA sample-memory read parameters.
Computes the circular-buffer start offset (settings+0x3c minus settings+0x2c), doubles it
when both channels are interleaved (settings[2]==1), writes the masked offset to register 3,
the capture length (settings+0x00) to register 0xb, the A/B cursor span (settings+0xd0/
+0xd2) + 1 to register 0xc, sets/clears bit 3 of mode register 2 from param_1, then issues
command 0x10 to register 1.

name: zw_fpga_check_trigger_occurred
comment: Return the FPGA 'trigger occurred' status flag: bit 0 of SPI status register 0x0f.

name: zw_fpga_check_maxmin_ready
comment: Return the FPGA 'max/min capture ready' status flag: bit 1 of SPI status register 0x0f.

name: zw_fpga_read_data_from_memory
comment: Read acquired samples from FPGA sample memory over hardware SPI: program registers 0x16/3, set stream-enable bit 0x20 (and bit 3 depending on mode), start with register 2, receive param_3 bytes in 1000-byte chunks via zw_spi_receive_hw with param_5-scaled delays, then disable streaming.

name: zw_gray_init
comment: Initialise the four trace-render descriptors (CH1/CH2 live and persistence buffers) with channel IDs 0/1 and palette colour indices 0x3F/0x5F.

name: zw_scope_transfer_maxmin_data
comment: Transfers the min/max sample pairs for the visible window over SPI: waits for the FPGA max/min-ready flags for bank 0 and bank 1 (zw_fpga_set_data_read_params 0/1), reads two bytes per sample into 600-byte buffers at the window offset, and merges them for the renderer. Called from zw_scope_prepare_display_data and its zoom variant.

name: zw_scope_process_samples_for_rendering
comment: Turns acquired samples into display data: interpolates when roll mode is active (settings[0xDF]) or refreshes the raw display buffers, then downsamples each screen column according to the timebase ratio, writing both the main and persistence arrays. Called from zw_scope_prepare_display_data and its zoom variant.

name: zw_scope_apply_rendering_smoothing
comment: Smooths the rendered 300-sample trace buffers: when the visible window is wider than 49 samples, applies a local 3-point median/average filter to remove single-pixel spikes in both channel arrays before finalization. Called by zw_scope_finalize_render_buffer.

name: zw_scope_finalize_render_buffer
comment: Finalizes a rendered channel buffer after smoothing: normalizes/clamps the sample values using the channel offset and gain, computes the buffer min/max statistics, and stores them in the buffer header (bytes 4/5). Called from zw_scope_prepare_display_data and its zoom variant.

name: zw_scope_handle_auto_trace_centering
comment: Auto-centers a channel trace vertically when the trace mean drifts from screen center: averages the two trace banks, computes a bounded correction step, and adjusts the CH1 offset settings +0x48 or CH2 offset +0x88, forcing a re-render when the offset changes. Called from zw_scope_prepare_display_data and its zoom variant.

name: zw_scope_prepare_display_data
comment: Builds the time-domain display buffers each frame: transfers max/min pairs or processes raw samples, finalizes and auto-centers the CH1/CH2 buffers, and maintains the 300-sample history ring used by roll and persistence rendering. Called from main.

name: zw_screenshot_copy_fb_to_buffer
comment: Copy four 300-byte slices of the framebuffer (two source pointers, each with a 300-byte pair) into the screenshot staging buffer at offsets +0/+15000/+30000/+45000 and clear the busy flag. Used by the screenshot save path.

name: zw_scope_draw_trace_to_framebuffer
comment: Plots one channel's trace into the 8-bpp framebuffer from the min/max sample banks: for each sample column fills the vertical span min..max with the palette color (param_1 high byte), offset by the plot origin (10,10) and clipped to the 200-row plot area. Called by zw_scope_persistence.

name: zw_scope_persistence
comment: Renders the main and persistence traces: fades the previous framebuffer in persistence mode, draws the grayscale persistence layer when enabled (settings[0xE6]/[0x129]), otherwise copies and plots the channel buffers with their palette colors. Called from zw_scope_ui_refresh when not in the zoom overlay mode.

name: zw_scope_prepare_display_data_zoom
comment:
Builds the zoomed display buffers.
When not in XY mode and the right cursor is before column 300, it processes the samples
into min/max buffers for the current time base, then temporarily swaps settings[0x10] with
the saved zoom time base (settings[0x134]), zeroes the roll flag, recalculates timing and
processes the same samples again, restoring the original time base afterwards. CH2 is
processed too in dual-channel mode.

name: zw_scope_draw_trace_dual_ch
comment:
Renders the dual-channel waveform into the framebuffer.
For every column x in the cursor range settings+0xd0..+d2 it fills the min..max sample span
of the selected channel (low byte of param_1: 0=CH1, 1=CH2) with palette color
param_1>>16, at framebuffer row (sample>>1)+4, column x+10.

name: zw_scope_draw_persistence_trace
comment:
Renders the persistence (afterglow) traces into the framebuffer.
For every column x in the A/B cursor range (settings+0xd0..+d2) it fills the column's
min..max sample span (arrays at the two sample-buffer pointers) with palette color
param_1>>16, at row (sample>>1)+0x68 and column x+10. Low byte of param_1 selects the
channel (0=CH1, 1=CH2).

name: zw_scope_render_all_traces
comment: Renders all trace layers for the current view: the dual-channel trace for the main and, when enabled, the persistence/zoom buffers selected by settings[+0x11E] and settings[2]. Each 0x4A6-byte display buffer is copied to the stack before being drawn. Called from zw_scope_ui_refresh.

name: zw_zoom_mode_handler
comment:
Zoom-mode (time-base magnification) handler.
Action 0x4d toggles the zoom-mode flag settings[0x129] and re-applies hardware settings.
Action 0x4a toggles zoom: when settings[0x135] is set, the previously saved time-base
offsets (settings+0x6c, +0xac) are restored and the flag cleared; otherwise, if no popup or
menu is active and the time-base index is in the zoomable range, the current offsets are
saved, the time base is scaled, and hardware is updated. Invalid requests show the 'Limit'
popup (zw_draw_popup_message).

name: zw_scope_exit_zoom_mode_and_update
comment:
Leave zoom mode from a non-zoom UI path: if the zoom-active flag settings[0x135] is set,
clears it, restores the saved time-base offsets settings+0x6c and settings+0xac from the backup
at 0x2001a614/0x20019c9c, and re-applies hardware settings (mask 0xff).

name: zw_scope_calculate_and_draw_math_trace
comment: Computes and draws the MATH trace (CH1+CH2, CH1-CH2 or inverted, selected by settings[0x148]) when math display is enabled and neither cursor, zoom nor CH2-only view is active. Combines the two 300-sample buffers into the math buffer and plots the result. Called from zw_scope_ui_refresh.

name: zw_scope_draw_trigger_icon
comment: Draws a small trigger-mode icon as an 8x8 dot pattern directly into LCD controller RAM (RGB565 color 0x07E0) at one of the home-screen grid cells: param_1 low 2 bits select the column, upper bits the row. Called from zw_home_screen.

name: zw_home_screen
comment: Handles the Home icon menu: event 1 toggles between the normal scope view (settings[1] 1) and the home page (settings[1] 7), drawing the 320x240 Home bitmap and trigger icon; navigation events move among the five home icons and return the selected action code. Called from main.

name: zw_scope_fetch_samples_from_fpga
comment: Acquire a fresh sample set from the FPGA and store it in the CH1/CH2 waveform buffers (0x2001D2A0 / 0x2001A618), applying the current channel mode, trigger position and roll-mode handling. Runs from the main acquisition loop while the scope is running.

name: zw_scope_update_display_buffers
comment:
Recompute how many samples to fetch for display: reads the float time-base value at
settings+0xd4, multiplies by 300.0 and 100.0, truncates to unsigned, rounds up to a multiple of
100 (ceil(v/100)) and calls zw_scope_fetch_samples_from_fpga with that count.

name: zw_scope_apply_dsp_filter
comment: DSP resampling/filter helper for traces: computes the per-pixel ratio from the sample count and timebase, resamples/interpolates the source buffer into the destination, and optionally processes both channels; used by interpolated rendering and the software trigger search.

name: zw_scope_software_trigger_search
comment:
Software trigger search over the CH1 sample buffer.
Maps the analog trigger level (settings+0x40, or +0x126 in roll mode) to a +/-2 pixel band,
fetches the pre-trigger window from FPGA memory into ch1_DAT_0x2001d2a0, applies the DSP
filter, then scans for a rising or falling edge through the band according to the edge
setting settings[0x3a]. On success the trigger sample index is stored in the global
trigger-position variable.

name: zw_scope_align_sampled_data
comment:
Aligns the sampled data to the trigger position.
Computes the sample offset from the trigger position and the time base, then copies 300
bytes of CH1 from the raw buffer+offset to the aligned output buffer. In dual-channel mode
it also copies 300 bytes of CH2, adding a phase offset of 10/4/2 samples for sample rates
of 10/20/50 (interleaving compensation).

name: zw_scope_generate_interpolated_traces
comment:
Builds the interpolated CH1/CH2 sample buffers for the current time base.
Matches settings+0xe0 against an 8-entry time-base table to pick a fixed start offset
(default 0x14b), stores the sample rate (1e6/timebase) in a global, runs the software
trigger search, fetches the window from FPGA memory, applies the DSP filter to CH1 (and
CH2 in dual mode), then aligns the data and advances a 0..9 frame-rotation counter.

name: zw_scope_fetch_samples_generic
comment:
Generic FPGA sample fetch used by the rendering path (param_1 = extra sample offset,
param_2 = byte count). Converts the 64-bit timestamp settings+0x30 to samples with
__divdi3/__moddi3 by 1000, derives the circular read offset from settings+0x3c, wraps it
by the buffer length settings+0xc, then reads CH1 (and CH2 when dual-channel) through
zw_fpga_read_data_from_memory.

name: zw_scope_measure_vpp_avg_rms
comment: Computes vertical statistics for one channel over the capture buffer: min/max, average and RMS. Raw 8-bit samples are converted to engineering units with the channel offset/gain stored in settings (+0x44/+0x74/+0x78 for CH1, +0x84/+0xB4/+0xB8 for CH2). Writes Vpp/Vtop/Vbase, Vavg and Vrms into the measurement block. param_3 selects the channel, param_4 packs flags and the sample count.

name: zw_scope_measure_top_base_amp
comment: Estimates the top and base levels of a waveform by histogram-style scanning: it counts occurrences of levels near the upper and lower extremes of the min/max range and picks the most frequent ones. Derives amplitude = top - base. Called for a channel when measurement flags (+0x6C/+0xAC) request top/base/amplitude.

name: zw_scope_measure_frequency_and_duty
comment: Measure frequency and duty from an 8-bit trace using hysteresis-threshold edge detection. Finds up to 100 rising/falling edges, averages the counted periods, converts to time using the sample interval in settings +0x14/+0x18, and stores frequency and duty in the measurement result block (+0x40/+0x48). param_4 packs the low/high hysteresis levels.

name: zw_scope_measure_pulse_params
comment: Measure pulse parameters from an 8-bit trace: hysteresis-based edge detection collects up to 100 high/low run lengths, computes average high and low widths, period/frequency (+0x50/+0x58) and duty percentages in 0.1% units (+0x60/+0x62); also calls zw_scope_measure_frequency_and_duty when the channel is configured for frequency display.

name: zw_scope_measurements
comment: Main measurement pass, called from main once per frame. In roll mode it measures the 300-sample snapshot at PTR_DAT_0801A8CC; otherwise it derives the visible sample window and decimation from settings +0xC0..+0xD2. Runs zw_scope_measure_vpp_avg_rms, zw_scope_measure_pulse_params and (when flags +0x6C/+0xAC bit 0x10 are set) zw_scope_measure_top_base_amp for CH1 and CH2, filling the measurement block consumed by the label renderer.

name: zw_scope_measurement_labels
comment: Renders the on-screen measurement panel. Formats per-channel frequency, Vpp, Vavg, Vrms, period, duty cycle and pulse width and draws them into a 3-column, multi-row grid using the small font (Chinese glyphs at 0x08028C24, English strings otherwise). param_26 != 0 selects CH2; row/column tables and the measurement-enable flags live in settings +0x69/+0x6C/+0xA9/+0xAC and +0x108/+0x10A. Called from zw_scope_update_measurement_labels.

name: zw_scope_update_measurement_labels
comment:
Refresh the on-screen measurement labels: zeroes the dirty flags, copies the 0x54-byte
CH1 label descriptor from +0x10 of the measurement state to the stack, calls
zw_scope_measurement_labels with its first four fields (recomputing Vpp/freq/etc.), bumps the
label sequence counter, and repeats for CH2 when dual-channel display is enabled (settings[2]==1).

name: zw_scope_draw_trigger_state_icon
comment:
Draw the trigger-state icon when enabled: if settings[0x121] bit 3 is set, renders the
parametrized trigger glyph from the UI element at 0x20002a70.

name: zw_scope_center_ch1_trace
comment:
Centers the CH1 trace vertically.
If settings[0x68]==1 (auto/AC) the channel offset is zeroed; otherwise computes a 64-bit
offset adjustment from the CH1 scale settings+0x44, the current offset settings+0x48 and the
ADC midpoint, storing it at settings+0x54/+0x58. In normal trigger mode it saves the
trigger position and re-bases settings+0x7c; in roll mode those are zeroed. Sets the
vertical position to 0 and re-applies hardware settings.

name: zw_scope_center_ch2_trace
comment:
Centers the CH2 trace vertically.
If settings[0xa8]==1 (auto/AC) the channel offset is zeroed; otherwise computes a 64-bit
offset adjustment from the CH2 scale settings+0x84, the current offset settings+0x88 and the
ADC midpoint, storing it at settings+0x94/+0x98. In normal trigger mode it also saves the
trigger position and re-bases settings+0xbc; in roll mode those are zeroed. Finally sets the
vertical position to 5 and re-applies hardware settings.

name: zw_center_channel_handler
comment:
Handle channel-centering keys: key 0x14 vertically centers CH1 and key 0x54 centers CH2
(zeroing that channel's vertical offset). Returns the key code so the caller sees it consumed.

name: zw_scope_calculate_ch1_auto_trigger
comment:
Compute the CH1 vertical offset used by auto-setup: unless settings[0x68]==1 (special
coupling/invert case), offset = settings+0x44 scale * ((average ADC - 0x7F) - param) / 25; stores
the value at settings+0x54 and its sign extension at +0x58. Zeroes both otherwise.

name: zw_scope_calculate_ch2_auto_trigger
comment:
Compute the CH2 vertical offset used by auto-setup: unless settings[0xa8]==1, offset =
settings+0x84 scale * ((average ADC - 0x80) - param) / 25; stores the value at settings+0x94 and
its sign extension at +0x98. Zeroes both otherwise.

name: zw_auto_trigger_level_calculation
comment: Computes the automatic trigger level from the midpoint between the captured trace minimum and maximum, converts it through the channel offset/gain, and writes it into the trigger settings. Runs at a throttled rate while AUTO trigger is active; called from main.

name: zw_scope_save_waveform_buffer
comment: Snapshot 300 samples of both channels (live and alternate arrays) plus the display window start/end columns when the Save key (0x52) arms it; the saved trace is then drawn by zw_scope_draw_saved_waveform.

name: zw_scope_draw_saved_waveform
comment: Draw the saved waveform snapshot into the LCD framebuffer: CH1 envelope in color 2 and CH2 (when enabled) in color 4, with the y range clipped to rows 0x1C..0xE3 and the trace window offset by 10 pixels.

name: zw_scope_auto_adc_interleave_check
comment:
Periodic auto ADC interleave (dual-ADC phase) check, called from the main loop.
When its timer expires it sets the FPGA ADC interleave mode from settings[0x38] && settings[2]
(both non-zero => interleave on), samples both ADC values, and raises the mismatch flag at the
pointer target when |chA-chB| >= 26 and, if settings[0x3b] is set, the per-channel threshold at
settings+0x40 does not lie between the two readings. Flag=0 when values look consistent.

name: zw_scope_acq_state_machine
comment: Scope acquisition state machine, called from main every loop. State is kept in settings[0xDC]: 0 idle, 1 arm/settle delay, 2 wait-for-trigger, 3 stop, 0xFF timeout. Arms the FPGA in single or continuous mode, polls the trigger (zw_fpga_check_trigger_occurred), enforces auto-trigger timeouts, handles roll/block and interleaved-ADC configurations, and stops the acquisition when requested.

name: zw_settings_save
comment: Saves settings: copies the first 0x154 bytes of global_settings into a 0x400-byte buffer, appends 'GO' validity magic at +0x3FE, then writes to flash at (0x96000 + offset). All callers pass offset 0x1000 -> absolute 0x08097000.

name: zw_settings_load
comment: Loads a 0x400-byte settings record from flash (0x96000 + offset; caller passes 0x1000 -> 0x08097000) and accepts it only if the 'GO' magic is present at +0x3FE.

name: zw_settings_invalidate
comment: Invalidates saved settings by clearing the 'GO' magic and rewriting the 0x400-byte record at flash (0x96000 + offset); caller passes 0x1000 -> 0x08097000.

name: zw_screenshot_view
comment:
Displays stored screenshot imgSel. Looks up the flash slot in screenshot_index_buffer,
reads the 2048-byte record at 0x08096000 + (slot+0x54)*0x800, restores the recorded
waveform arrays and 340-byte settings snapshot, redraws the scope UI with that state,
overlays 'imgSel+1/total' and flushes. Previous settings are saved/restored around it.

name: zw_screenshot_init
comment:
Initializes the screenshot system: arms a 90 ms timer, reads the 136-byte screenshot index
from flash offset 0x29000 (persistent area 0x96000), and if the count/max fields are invalid
resets it to 63 empty slots and writes it back. Then sets up the image-browser UI elements:
zoom at (299,135), trash at (300,183) and exit at (295,219).

name: zw_screenshot_save
comment: Saves a screenshot: writes the 0x800-byte image to slot n at absolute 0x080C0000 + n*0x800 and updates the 0x88-byte index at 0x080BF000.

name: zw_screenshot_render_envelope
comment:
Renders a 75-column min/max envelope of the waveforms into a screenshot bitmap.
Decimates the sample arrays by 4, tracks the min/max of each column (local_c0/local_74),
then draws vertical lines with zw_draw_vline_indexed at x=param_1.., y offset param_2,
compressed by /5, using color param_5. Used when composing screenshots of the traces.

name: zw_screenshot_draw_thumbnail
comment:
Draws screenshot browser entry param_3 as a thumbnail at (x=param_1, y=param_2).
Reads its 2048-byte record and renders the stored trace envelopes: first pair with
palette index 0x3F (CH1 color) and second pair with 0x5F (CH2 color); the saved enable
flags at record offsets 0x4B2/0x5CE decide which pairs are drawn.

name: zw_screenshot_browser
comment: Screenshot browser and save path: stores the current screen into the flash screenshot ring (63 records of 0x800 bytes from 0x08096000+0x2A000), navigates the thumbnail grid, opens a screenshot, and deletes entries via zw_screenshot_delete_handler. Maintains the 340-byte settings snapshot so that leaving the browser restores the previous instrument state. Called from main.

name: zw_scope_ch1_set_trigger_level
comment: Adjusts the CH1 trigger level from front-panel events 0x25/0x26: moves the level as a fraction (1/25) of the CH1 vertical scale settings[0x44], clamps it to the channel range and refreshes the trigger-level display. Called from zw_scope_apply_settings_update.

name: zw_scope_ch2_set_trigger_level
comment: Adjusts the CH2 trigger level from front-panel events 0x27/0x28: moves the level as a fraction of the vertical scale settings[0x84], clamps it to the channel range and refreshes the trigger-level display. Called from zw_scope_apply_settings_update.

name: zw_scope_ch1_vertical_handler
comment: Vertical front-panel handler for CH1. V/div events 0x15/0x16 move the sensitivity index settings[0x42] through the 14-entry table (clamped at 4..13) with 'Limit' popups; position events 0x21/0x22 adjust settings +0x44/+0x4C..+0x50 within bounds and update the AFE offset, displaying the value. Called from zw_scope_apply_settings_update.

name: zw_scope_ch2_vertical_handler
comment: Vertical front-panel handler for CH2. V/div events 0x0D/0x05 move the sensitivity index settings[0x80] through the 14-entry table (clamped at 4..13) with 'Limit' popups; position events adjust settings +0x84/+0x8C within bounds and update the AFE offset, displaying the new value. Called from zw_scope_apply_settings_update.

name: zw_scope_set_math_vertical_offset
comment:
Adjusts the math trace vertical position from keys 0x31/0x32 (up/down).
Only active when math is enabled, settings[0x11e]==2 (math page) and no popup is open.
Changes the math offset settings+0x14c and the scaled position settings+0x150 by 1 or 2
steps (fine when settings[0x11f]/[0x130] set), clamping both to [-100,100].

name: zw_scope_horizontal_handler
comment: Horizontal front-panel handler. Event 0x11/0x12 (zoom keys) increments/decrements the timebase index settings[0x10] (0..29) using the 8-byte time/div table at 0x0801D994 and the per-channel limit settings[0x134]; the scroll events adjust horizontal position/trigger offset. Displays the new timebase via a temporary on-screen message. When settings[0x12B] is set it forces roll mode and clears the horizontal offsets.

name: zw_calculate_float_div_and_scale
comment: 64-bit scaled-division helper used by the timing calculations: divides the dividend param_1/param_2 by divisor param_3/param_4, applying 1000/1000000 pre-scaling and range checks, and returns the 32-bit quotient. Called from zw_scope_calculate_timing_params and zw_scope_memory_bar.

name: zw_scope_calculate_timing_params
comment: Derive all acquisition/display timing from the selected timebase: look up the sample interval and sample-count table for the time/div index, compute pre/post-trigger depths and trigger column, sample-window start/end offsets, roll-mode and interpolation flags, and update settings +0x14/+0x18 (sample interval), +0x1C (trigger offset), +0xC0 (sample rate divisor).

name: zw_scope_system_state_controller
comment: Handles global scope state transitions from front-panel events: RUN/STOP toggle (event 10) including run-state and horizontal-offset bookkeeping, auto-set, XY/display-mode switching and related status popups. Called from zw_scope_apply_settings_update.

name: zw_scope_apply_settings_update
comment: Apply pending settings to the hardware: system state, CH1/CH2 vertical stages, trigger levels, horizontal/timebase, math offset, timing recalculation, roll handling, PWM/backlight calibration and AFE re-initialisation; sets the redraw/refresh flags.

name: zw_scope_update_hardware_check
comment: Gate for applying pending settings to hardware: if a change is flagged (param != 0) and the instrument is in a scope-like mode (settings[1] == 1, 4 or 5), call zw_scope_apply_settings_update.

name: zw_scope_init_default_settings
comment: Load the settings block from flash; on first boot (no valid block) initialise all scope, siggen and calibration defaults, write DMM calibration defaults to flash offset 0x2400 and save the settings, then apply them to hardware. Uses factory defaults such as CH1/CH2 990000 gain and 5000 DMM counts.

name: zw_dmm_hv_relay_enable
comment:
Enable the DMM high-voltage relay by driving PA10 (GPIOA bit 10) high; used when selecting
high-voltage measurement ranges.

name: zw_dmm_side_menu
comment: Draws the DMM side menu strip along the right edge (0x28 px wide): five function buttons (V/mV, A/mA, resistance, continuity/diode, capacitance) separated by hairlines, with the active mode highlighted according to the current DMM mode. Called from zw_dmm_update.

name: zw_gpio_PA6_control
comment:
Drive PA6 as an output: configures PA6 (mask 0x40) as output and sets it high when
param != 0 or low when param == 0. Used by the DMM front-end control sequence.

name: zw_dmm_uart_init_hw
comment:
Initializes UART4 for the DMM module: 9600 baud, 8N1, no flow control, and arms
interrupt-driven receive into the DMM packet buffer. Handle uart4_init_data (0x2001DE58)
is serviced by UART1_IRQHandler together with the FPGA and voice UARTs.

name: zw_dmm_send_cmd
comment:
Sends a 10-byte command frame to the DMM MCU over UART4:
AA 55 <type> 00 00 00 00 <mode> <cksum_hi> <cksum_lo>, where checksum = type + mode
(16-bit). Called by the DMM mode/calibration logic with type 2 (self-test) and type 5
(mode select).

name: zw_dmm_set_hardware_mode
comment:
Selects a DMM frontend mode (0..11): writes the protocol mode byte to 0x200045A9,
configures PA10 range relay (bit 10) for modes 4/6 or enables the HV path relay for the
others, sends command 0x05 <mode>, then waits 100 ms. Mode byte map:
0:18 1:16 2:15 3:19 4:0A 5:0C 6:0B 7:0D 8:12 9:10 10:13 11:11; mode 2 also calls
zw_pwm_control_hw(0x31).

name: zw_dmm_frontend_init
comment:
Initialize the DMM front-end: configures the PA10 HV relay line as output, waits,
deasserts it, initializes the DMM UART, sets the front-end mode byte to 4, asserts PA6, waits
100 ms, arms a 280 ms settling timer, programs DMM hardware mode 4, and clears settings[0x131]
when the DMM is disabled (settings[0x12e]==0).

name: zw_dmm_factory_calibration
comment:
Factory DMM calibration state machine driven by key codes 0, 2, 0x0E, 0x0F, 0x13, 0x14:
runs self-inspection (cmd 2, 0xA0), then 100mV / 100mA / temperature calibration stages via
zw_dmm_send_cmd and frontend modes, showing prompts; marks settings[0x115] when done and
powers off at the end. Progress bytes at 0x200045A4/0x200045B0/0x200045D9.

name: zw_dmm_mode_handler
comment: Primary DMM input handler for DMM modes (settings[1] 1 or 7): toggles DMM on/off (events 0x18/0x58), selects measurement mode and unit, invokes zw_dmm_set_hardware_mode, and mirrors the selected mode over UART. Also manages auto-range state and warning popups.

name: zw_dmm_calib_mode
comment: Handles DMM calibration mode commands while the DMM view is open: entering via the 'c' key, saving (event 2) writes the 0x18-byte calibration block to flash at 0x08096000+0x2400, and reset (event 10) restores the 5000-count default and saves. Shows the DMM calibration and Save popups. Called from zw_dmm_update.

name: zw_7segment_to_digit
zw_dmm_parse_rx_packet
comment:
Decodes raw DMM measurement packets (header 5A A5). The 10-byte frame carries five
7-segment digit masks and unit/mode flag bytes; the routine converts the masks to digits,
extracts decimal-point position, AC/DC/auto and unit prefixes (K/M/m/n/u), then updates
the DMM display buffers and scaled measurement value. Also used for the data shown in the
DMM view and for calibration readings.

name: zw_dmm_modes_menu_ui
comment: Redraws the DMM mode-selection grid: four columns by three rows of icons covering V/mV DC and AC, A/mA DC and AC, resistance, continuity, diode and capacitance, plus the selection frame for the current mode. Called by zw_dmm_setup_logic and zw_dmm_update.

name: zw_dmm_draw_digits_small_window
comment:
Draws the four digits of the DMM small window at (0xc2,0x2c) using the 24x28 DMM digit
font (color 5, transparent background). Decimal points are inserted after digits 3..0
according to the dmm_dp_0 flags.

name: zw_dmm_draw_window_digits
comment: Draws the DMM reading digits inside the small function window with the 24x28 font: minus sign, decimal points according to the active range and all four digits; special/over-range readings are delegated to zw_dmm_draw_digits_small_window. Called by zw_dmm_window.

name: zw_dmm_window
comment: Draws the DMM function window in the upper-right corner: range text for the active mode (DC 1000V/600mV, AC 750V/600mV, DC 10A/600mA, AC 10A/600mA) or the resistance/continuity/diode/capacitance icon, then the formatted reading via zw_dmm_draw_window_digits, plus high-voltage and ohm indicators.

name: zw_dmm_format_special_value
comment: Renders special DMM values (over-range/OL, blank or invalid digits) as 40x81 glyphs and appends the same characters to the UART TX buffer: non-decimal digit codes become spaces or '-', and decimal points are inserted per the active range. Called by zw_dmm_format_measurement for readings that are not normal 4-digit values.

name: zw_dmm_format_measurement
comment: Formats the current DMM reading into large 40x81 digit glyphs: minus sign, decimal point according to the active range, all four digits and special/over-range values via zw_dmm_format_special_value, while appending the same characters to the UART TX buffer for the remote display. Called by zw_dmm_fullscreen.

name: zw_dmm_fullscreen
comment: Renders the full-screen DMM page: title bar, the formatted reading from zw_dmm_format_measurement, large unit symbols (V/mV/A/mA DC or AC, resistance, continuity, diode, capacitance) chosen by the active mode, range hints (e.g. 'Max 1000V') and battery status. Called from zw_dmm_update while the DMM view is active.

name: zw_dmm_setup_logic
zw_dmm_update
comment: DMM view update: redraws the full-screen or menu DMM page, parses the 10-byte 0x5AA5 measurement packet from UART4 when present, refreshes the battery icon, and dispatches factory-calibration and calibration sub-modes plus the jack image. Called from main and zw_dmm_calibration.

name: zw_dmm_calibration
comment: Interactive DMM calibration routine called from main: prompts for DCV 5.000V, resistance 100.0k, DCA and DCmA reference points, averages the DMM readings until the operator confirms each point, builds the 0x30-byte calibration block and writes it to flash at 0x08096000+0x2400.

name: zw_voice_uart_init_hw
comment:
Initialize the voice module's UART: instance 0x1000 (the third UART mapped on PA13), baud
rate 9600 (0x2580), 8 data bits configuration 3, then HAL_UART_Init and HAL_UART_Receive_IT into
the module's RX buffer (10-byte protocol frame).

name: zw_voice_module_power_control_hw
comment:
Control power to the voice-recognition module on PA14 (mask 0x4000): when param!=0,
configures PA14 as an output and drives it low (active-low enable); when param==0, restores PA14
to an input (module unpowered/high-Z).

name: zw_voice_control_init
comment:
Initialize the voice-command module. If settings[0x110] is 0, powers the module through
zw_voice_module_power_control_hw() (no forced state) and initializes its UART; otherwise calls
zw_voice_module_power_control_hw(1) to force power on first, then the same UART init.

name: zw_voice_control
comment: Voice-recognition module handler (separate UART). Command 0x55 toggles voice control (settings[0x110], with Voice ON/OFF popup). While enabled, an 0xA1-prefixed frame is decoded into a key action: 0x88 power off, 0x10-0x15 run/single/X-Y/back, 0x20/0x21 coupling, 0x32 trigger source, 0x40/0x41 menu/view, 0x43 generator, 0x45 50%, 0x46 CH2, 0x50-0x57 scope controls, 0x60-0x66 DMM modes. Returns the key code to the main UI loop.

name: zw_voice_timer_start
comment:
Arm the voice-control polling timer: sets a 200 ms one-shot timer (zw_timer_us). The main
loop later checks it to poll the voice/command front-end.

name: zw_auto_setup_step_ch1_vertical
comment: One step of the AUTO-set vertical routine for CH1: selects non-interleaved CH1 sampling, samples CH1 min/max via zw_fpga_read_adc_values, converts the levels through the vertical gain table indexed by settings[0x42], and chooses the scale/offset that centers the trace. Returns 0 while waiting or when the step completes; called from zw_auto_setup_handler.

name: zw_auto_setup_step_ch2_vertical
comment: One step of the AUTO-set vertical routine for CH2: enables ADC interleave, samples CH2 min/max through zw_fpga_read_adc_values, converts the levels through the vertical gain table indexed by settings[0x80], and selects the scale/offset that centers the trace. Returns 0 while waiting or when the step completes; called from zw_auto_setup_handler.

name: zw_auto_setup_step_ch1_horizontal
comment:
Auto-setup horizontal step for CH1.
State 0 saves the current trigger mode/source, forces source 0 / mode 1 with a preset auto
trigger level, programs the trigger, disables ADC interleave and starts a 200 ms timer.
State 1 reads the FPGA edge count after the timer expires, restores the trigger mode, then
selects a time-base index: <2 edges restores the previous setting and uses index 0x0e,
otherwise it scans the time-base table at DAT_08022720 for the fastest base able to capture
the measured edge rate and applies it via zw_scope_update_hardware_check(0xff).

name: zw_auto_setup_step_ch2_horizontal
comment:
Auto-setup horizontal step for CH2 (same sequence as the CH1 variant).
State 0 saves trigger mode/source, forces source 1 / mode 1 with a preset auto trigger
level, enables ADC interleave and starts a 200 ms timer. State 1 reads the FPGA edge count,
restores the trigger mode and, when more than one edge was seen, scans the time-base table
to pick a suitable time base (0x03..0x17) and applies it via
zw_scope_update_hardware_check(0xff).

name: zw_auto_setup_handler
comment: AUTO-set state machine, called from main. While settings[1]==4 it arms the FPGA/ADC interleave, reads CH1 and CH2 levels, centers the traces, runs the vertical steps for CH1/CH2 and the horizontal timebase step, and finally computes auto trigger levels. Event 0x60 starts AUTO, event 0x20 aborts; shows an AUTO status popup.

name: zw_personalization_menu_handler
comment: Input handler for the personalization menu (settings page 8). Scrolls a 13-entry option list with up/down and fast-scroll events, redraws the preview page on open (event 0x7F), applies color/theme, LCD invert and backlight choices, and repaints the affected screen regions using the indexed framebuffer and image elements. param_1 is the key/event code.

name: zw_scope_fetch_samples_for_persistence
comment:
Fetches the samples used for the persistence (afterglow) display.
Computes the circular start offset like zw_fpga_set_data_read_params (doubled for
interleaved dual channel), derives the sample count from the cursor span times the sample
density settings+0x00, splits large captures into ceil(n/6000) equal chunks, stores the
resulting sample interval in a global, and reads CH1 (and CH2 in dual mode) from FPGA
memory in those chunks through zw_fpga_read_data_from_memory. A state byte is then copied
within the persistence UI buffer at +0x76e/+0x76f.

name: zw_scope_process_grayscale_persistence
comment: Builds the grayscale persistence histogram for the current capture: updates a 300x200 hit-count array from the trace buffers, tracks the illumination range and color mapping, and hands the result to zw_scope_draw_grayscale_trace. Called from zw_scope_prepare_display_data when grayscale persistence is enabled (settings[0xE6]).

name: zw_scope_draw_grayscale_trace
comment:
Grayscale persistence pass: for each column in the cursor range and each of the 200 rows,
adds the per-pixel persistence accumulator (buffer300_a) scaled by a brightness factor
(0x40 / intensity, recomputed each frame) to the framebuffer, saturating at 0x60. Only
nonzero accumulator pixels are touched.

name: zw_siggen_waveform_gen
comment: Build the 256-sample DAC table for the selected signal-generator waveform (0 sine, 1 square, 2 triangle, 3 sawtooth, 4 half sine, 5 full-wave rectified sine, 6 sinc table, 7 noise, 0xFF off) and load it into the FPGA wave buffer.

name: zw_siggen_init
comment:
Initializes the signal-generator UI: window element at (0x55,0x57), fullscreen frequency
text, on/off indicator and waveform/scope icons. Applies the configured frequency/duty
(settings+0xf0/+0xec), regenerates the waveform when enabled (settings[0xea]) and updates
the enable control.

name: zw_siggen_overlay_handler
comment: Keypad handler for the signal-generator overlay. Up/down selects the waveform index (0..8: sine, square, triangle, sawtooth, half sine, full-wave rectified, sinc, noise, off), left/right adjusts the active numeric field, and OK/event 0x7E enables the output. Frequency range (Hz/kHz/MHz) is recomputed from settings +0xF0 into the display globals; edits are applied through zw_siggen_freq_duty and zw_siggen_waveform_gen.

name: zw_scope_siggen_window
