comment: Draws the small signal-generator status window in the normal scope view: waveform icon, 7-segment frequency digits with the active digit highlighted, and the output-on indicator. Visible when settings[0x121] bit 2 is set; called from zw_scope_ui_refresh and zw_scope_redraw_frame.

name: zw_siggen_key_handler
comment: Signal-generator key handling: change waveform, frequency, amplitude and on/off state, update the generator display and reload the DAC table when the waveform changes.

name: zw_siggen_fullscreen
comment: Renders the fullscreen signal-generator page when settings[0x12D] is enabled: clears the 8-bpp framebuffer, draws title, battery status, waveform icon, frequency in 32x53 digits, duty cycle in 7-segment digits and amplitude/offset fields with the selected-field highlight. Called from main.

name: zw_measurement_ui_init
comment:
Initialize the measurement UI state: sets the 1,000,000 base scale, zero value, display
thresholds (0xd2,0x18,5,0,6), enables two state bytes, and arms the 300 ms, 1.5 s and 50 ms
timers used by the measurement update loop.

name: zw_scope_frequency_meter
comment: Frequency-counter mode: measure the input frequency using the FPGA/timebase and the calibrated reference, then update the on-screen frequency reading.

name: zw_freq_meter_calibrate_reference
comment: Calibrate the frequency meter against the internal reference clock and store the correction factor used when converting counter values to Hz.

name: zw_freq_meter_handler
comment:
Frequency-counter gate handler.
Manages menu state settings[0x116]/[0x141] (page 4 entry/exit), enables the counter gate
(bit derived from settings[0]), programs the FPGA frequency-meter trigger levels around the
trigger level settings+0x40, resets and periodically polls the counter via
zw_fpga_read_counter(), storing the result in a global.

name: zw_scope_counter
comment:
Draws the frequency-counter popup: filled box at (0xb2,0x14), double dashed border, a
large 'C:' label and the counter value as a 10-digit decimal (clamped to 1999999999) in
large font. Only shown while the counter gate flag settings[0x141] is set.

name: zw_afe_get_relay_settings
comment:
Maps the requested AFE input range/impedance (10000, 20000, 40000, 100000 or 200000
ohm; values above the limit are divided by 50) to the three relay control bytes returned
through param_2/param_3/param_4. 10k=0,0,0; 20k=0,0,1; 40k=0,1,0; 100k=1,0,0;
200k=1,0,1; any other value=0,1,1.

name: zw_HAL_init
comment:
Boot-time HAL bring-up: calls zw_HAL_msp_init (clocks/GPIO/peripherals) and arms a 20 ms
timer used by the early startup state machine.

name: zw_fpga_set_afe_offset_dac
comment:
Program the AFE offset DACs: converts both inputs (20.12-style fixed point, dividing by
the upper 12 bits after a <<12 scaling) to 12-bit values clamped at 0xFFF, then writes
(ch1 << 12) | ch2 to FPGA SPI register 0x13.

name: zw_scope_ch1_update_afe_offset
comment: Update only the CH1 vertical offset DAC (AFE serial word) without reconfiguring the relays.

name: zw_scope_ch1_afe_init
comment: Configure the CH1 analog front end for the current V/div and coupling: program attenuation relays and the offset DAC through the 24-bit bit-bang serial interface.

name: zw_scope_ch2_update_afe_offset
comment: Update only the CH2 vertical offset DAC (AFE serial word) without reconfiguring the relays.

name: zw_scope_ch2_afe_init
comment: Configure the CH2 analog front end for the current V/div and coupling: program attenuation relays and the offset DAC through the 24-bit bit-bang serial interface.

name: HAL_FLASH_Read_Offset_0x96000
comment:
Reads len bytes from serial flash at absolute address 0x08096000 + offset into buf.
Persistent layout: +0x0000 factory/UUID record, +0x1000 settings, +0x2000 scope
calibration, +0x2400 DMM calibration, +0x29000 screenshot index,
+0x2A000..+0x497FF screenshot records (63 x 0x800).

name: HAL_FLASH_Write_Offset_0x96000
comment: Writes a buffer to flash storage at 0x08096000 + offset. Storage map: +0x0000 factory/UUID (0x40); +0x1000 settings (0x400); +0x2000 scope calibration (0x8E); +0x2400 DMM calibration (0x18); +0x29000 screenshot index (0x88); +0x2A000..+0x497FF screenshot images (63 x 0x800).

name: low_level_init
comment: Early GPIO/ADC/timer initialization.

name: zw_lcd_backlight_enable_hw
comment:
Switch the LCD backlight enable line: drives PB27 (GPIOB bit 27, mask 0x08000000) high
when param != 0 and low when param == 0. Brightness is set separately by zw_lcd_set_pwm.

name: zw_battery_monitor
comment: Battery monitor: samples the battery voltage through the ADC every ~0.5 s, accumulates and averages readings, updates the battery icon, logs the value, periodically saves settings, and powers the instrument off below the low-battery threshold. Also samples the charge-detect GPIO. Called from main, zw_dmm_update and zw_siggen_fullscreen.

name: zw_draw_battery_icon_overlay
comment: Battery icon overlay. Uses the blink counter at 0x080256dc and the battery level at 0x080256e0. First erases the surrounding rectangle (0x122,4, 0x16x8). When the level is 2 (charging) the inner bar is alternately erased/filled from the counter bit 3 to create the blinking effect; otherwise it draws the battery frame at (0x123,5) size 0x11x6 and fills a bar whose width equals the level, using the colour word at 0x080256e4.

name: zw_gpio_PA6_read_hw
comment:
Read the PA6 key-matrix row: returns 3 when PA6 (GPIOA bit 6) is high, 0 otherwise. Called
by zw_keypress_scan/zw_keypress_handler when folding the third row into a key code.

name: zw_gpio_PA6_input
comment:
Reconfigure PA6 as an input: zw_gpio_init_hw(GPIOA, mask 0x40, pull=0, mode=2). Keeps the
key-matrix row readable after it was temporarily driven.

name: zw_afe_bitbang_write_24bit_hw
comment: Clock one 24-bit AFE control word out MSB-first: data on PB2, clock on PB3, latch on PA12, with a long delay between edges (about 800 cycles) to suit the slow serial AFE.

name: zw_HAL_msp_init
comment: Board-level MSP init: configure and clear the AFE bit-bang pins (PB2 data, PB3 clock, PA12 latch), set up PA4/PA5, program the two timer delays (15 ms) and clock out the initial 24-bit AFE word.

name: zw_scope_set_bandwidth_limit
comment:
Set the 20 MHz bandwidth limit for both channels. Clears bits 6 and 15 of the cached
24-bit AFE word, sets bit 6 (0x40) when ch1_limit_enable != 0, sets bit 15 (0x8000) when
ch2_limit_enable != 0, and bit-bangs the word to the AFE (filter relays).

name: zw_afe_set_ch1_enable_bit
comment:
Set/clear the CH1 AFE enable bit: param!=0 clears bit 7 (0x80) of the cached 24-bit AFE
control word, param==0 sets it, then pushes the word with zw_afe_bitbang_write_24bit_hw.
The bit is an active-low inhibit for the CH1 front-end.

name: zw_afe_pack_ch1_config
comment: Pack the CH1 analog front-end configuration into the 24-bit bit-banged word: the four config bytes are shifted into bits 1-4 of the word and the auxiliary bit into bit 5, preserving the other bits (~0x3E mask cleared first), then the word is clocked out to the AFE.

name: zw_afe_pack_ch2_config
comment: Pack the CH2 analog front-end configuration into the 24-bit bit-banged word: the four config bytes occupy bits 9-12 and the auxiliary bit bit 13, preserving the other fields (~0x3E00 mask cleared first), then the word is clocked out to the AFE.

name: zw_afe_set_ch2_enable_bit
comment:
Set/clear the CH2 AFE enable bit: param==0 clears bit 10 (0x400) of the cached 24-bit
AFE control word, param!=0 sets it, then pushes the word with zw_afe_bitbang_write_24bit_hw.
Opposite polarity to the CH1 enable helper: here 1 = enabled.

name: zw_power_off
comment: Controlled shutdown: save settings unless disabled, reset the AFE word, disable backlight and PWM, fill the LCD black and flush it, then cut power with zw_system_power_control(0) and hang until the next power-on/reset.

name: check_power_button_status
comment:
Return the power-button state: bit 21 (PB21) of the GPIOB data register; 1 = pressed/active.
Polled at boot to detect the power-on press and later the release.

name: zw_keypress_scan
comment:
Scans the front-panel key matrix.
Asserts the scan pattern through the AFE 24-bit bit-bang interface for each of 8 columns and
reads the row lines PA5, PA4 and PA6. Returns 0 when no key is pressed, otherwise
key code = 2 + column + row_offset with offsets 0 (PA5), 8 (PA4) and 16 (PA6).

name: zw_keypress_handler
comment: Keypad dispatch: translate scanned key events into scope, DMM, siggen and menu actions, track short/long-press flags and request the corresponding UI updates.

name: zw_power_button_logic_handler
comment: Power-key state machine sampled by the key timer: debounce the power button, distinguish a short press from a long hold (>30 ticks), inject key 0x81 and run the on/off cycle on a long hold.

name: zw_key_event_to_action
comment: Converts a raw keypad event into a scope action code according to the current UI state (normal view, menu, DMM, browser, zoom), handling short/long presses, RUN/STOP, menu navigation and the channel/trigger quick keys. Returns 0 when the event is consumed without an action. Called from main and zw_dmm_calibration.

name: st7789_write_command_hw
comment:
Send an 8-bit command to the ST7789 over the parallel bus: writes the command byte to the
GPIOB data register (PB0-PB15 data, RS=0, CS held low by the caller), then pulses WR (PB18,
0x40000) high and low. Used during init when the backlight is still off.

name: st7789_cs_low_hw
comment:
Assert the ST7789 chip select (PB26 low): clears bit 26 (0x04000000) of the GPIOB data
register 0x40011400, then refreshes the cached GPIOB output image at 0x200047a8.

name: st7789_cs_high_hw
comment:
Deassert the ST7789 chip select (PB26 high): sets bit 26 (0x04000000) of the GPIOB data
register 0x40011400.

name: st7789_write_data_16bit_hw
comment:
Writes one RGB565 pixel over the 16-bit parallel bus PB0-PB15. Preserves the upper
GPIOB lines, drives the pixel value, then pulses WR (PB18). RS (PB22) and CS (PB26) must
already be in the data state; used by pixel-streaming loops.

name: st7789_init_sequence_hw
comment: Bit-bangs the ST7789 initialization sequence over the 16-bit parallel GPIOB bus: soft reset 0xFE/0xEF, MADCTL 0x36 (rotation), pixel format 0x3A, porch/gamma/power registers, inversion selection (settings[0x114]) and sleep-out/display-on, with HAL_Delay waits. Called by zw_lcd_hard_init.

name: zw_lcd_hard_init
comment: Hardware bring-up of the LCD interface: configures all GPIOB ST7789 pins as outputs, waits 50 ms, drives CS/WR/RS high, waits another 10 ms, then runs the ST7789 initialisation command sequence.

name: zw_lcd_set_invert_mode_hw
comment:
Sends ST7789 display-inversion command: INVON (0x21) when arg==0, INVOFF (0x20)
otherwise, with WR strobe; returns CS and RS high afterwards. Used by the display
settings menu.

name: st7789_set_address_window_hw
comment:
Sets the ST7789 drawing window (column/row address range) over the 16-bit parallel bus.
Sends command 0x2A (CASET) with param_1..param_1+param_3-1, then 0x2B (RASET) with
positionY..positionY+height-1, high byte first; each byte is clocked via GPIOB with
WR/RS toggling (the repeated |0x400000/|0x440000 writes).

name: zw_draw_hline_indexed_hw_fast
comment: Fast horizontal line that bypasses the framebuffer: programs the ST7789 column/row window, issues RAMWR (0x2C) and bit-bangs each 16-bit pixel directly onto the GPIOB data register (the 0x40000 bit toggles WR).

name: zw_draw_vline_indexed_hw_fast
comment: Fast vertical line that bypasses the framebuffer: same ST7789 window + RAMWR (0x2C) path as the fast hline, with a 1-pixel-wide, h-tall window and each pixel bit-banged straight to the panel.

name: zw_lcd_fill_rect_rgb565
comment:
Fills a rectangle with one RGB565 color: programs the address window (x, y, width,
height) with 0x2A/0x2B, sends RAMWR (0x2C) and streams width*height identical pixels with
WR strobes while CS is low; CS returns high after the transfer. Used for clearing and
solid UI panels (the scope trace UI uses the indexed framebuffer path instead).

name: zw_draw_bitmap
comment:
Blits a 16bpp RGB565 image directly to the ST7789 over the parallel bus.
Sets the address window at (param_2,param_3) with the given width/height, sends 0x2C
(RAMWR), asserts CS low, streams width*height 16-bit pixels from imageData (each written
twice, once with the WR strobe bit 0x40000), then deasserts CS.

name: zw_draw_element_16bpp
comment:
Blits a 16bpp image with a 2-word header (width, height at param_1[0..1]; pixels follow)
to the ST7789 at (param_2,param_3). Sets the window, sends 0x2C, asserts CS, streams the
pixels over the parallel bus and releases CS.

name: SPIFLS_Init
comment: Initialise the SPI instance used by the flash driver (handle at 0x400): fills the SPI handle fields, calls HAL_SPI_Init, reads the flash JEDEC ID via fls_drv_read_id and enables the flash/SPI clock (0x40000E00 |= 0x100).

name: zw_fpga_spi_write_reg
comment: Write one FPGA configuration register over hardware SPI: 5-byte frame of (reg & 0x7F) followed by the 32-bit value big-endian. Bit 2 of the shared SPI control word is cleared before the transfer and set afterwards.

name: zw_fpga_spi_read_reg
comment: Read a 32-bit FPGA register over the bit-banged SPI bus: sends the register number with the read flag (reg | 0x80), receives 4 bytes, toggles SPI control bit 2 around the transfer and returns the received word with revb applied (byte order corrected).

name: zw_spi_read_samples_hw
comment: Read a block of ADC samples from the FPGA: rejects sizes above 1000, sends command 0x8A and receives Size bytes through the SPI interface.

name: zw_spi_start_sample_transfer_hw
comment:
Start the SPI sample-transfer engine: clears bit 2 of the SPI control register and
transmits the single command byte 0x8a. Counterpart of zw_spi_stop_sample_transfer_hw; the
FPGA then streams acquisition data.

name: zw_spi_receive_hw
comment:
Receive Size bytes over the ST7789/FPGA SPI bus with a 5 s timeout: HAL_SPI_Receive(hspi,
pData, Size, 5000). Used for FPGA register reads and panel status reads.

name: zw_spi_stop_sample_transfer_hw
comment:
Abort the SPI sample-transfer engine: sets bit 2 of the SPI instance's control register
(hspi->Instance->CR1), stopping any in-flight bulk transfer.

name: zw_fft_compute
comment: Compute the 1024-point FFT of the displayed channel trace: convert 8-bit samples into complex bins, run the radix-2 transform and derive the magnitudes used by the FFT view.

name: zw_fft_handler
comment: FFT display handler: when the FFT-enable flag in the settings block (offset 0xFC) is set, calls zw_fft_compute on the current acquisition buffer and maps/normalises the first 300 FFT bins into the display value range for drawing.

name: zw_fft_draw_bars_visualizer
comment: Render the FFT magnitudes as vertical bars; heights are capped at 0x95 and scaled specially according to settings[0xFC] (bar modes 2/3).

name: zw_fft_draw_trace_mode
comment: Render the FFT magnitudes as a connected trace over the graticule; used when settings[0xFC] selects trace mode 0.

name: printf_disabled_1
comment: Disabled printf variant 1: empty variadic stub (compiled-out diagnostic print).

name: zw_delay_cycles_small_hw
comment:
Short calibrated busy-wait: loops (cycles>>5) times. Used for tightly-timed bit-banging
(e.g. AFE serial clocks) where tick-based delays are too coarse.

name: zw_delay_cycles_large_hw
comment:
Long calibrated busy-wait: loops (cycles*120) times. Same purpose as
zw_delay_cycles_small_hw for microsecond-scale waits in bit-banged protocols.

name: HAL_Delay
comment: HAL tick-based millisecond delay: busy-waits until HAL_GetTick() advances by Delay ms.

name: zw_timer_us
comment: Software timer helper in microseconds: rounds the requested period up to whole milliseconds with a minimum of 1 ms, samples HAL_GetTick and stores {last_tick, period_ms} in the two-word timer state.

name: zw_timer_check
comment:
Non-blocking timer check: param_1 points to {last_tick, period_ms}. Returns 0 while
(now - last_tick) < period; when elapsed, stores now in last_tick and returns 1. Backs all the
periodic UI/measurement polls and the popup timeout.

name: zw_list_insert_top
comment: Insert a 16-bit entry at the top of a fixed-capacity list (capacity at +0x80, count at +0x84, entry array at +0): shifts the existing entries one slot toward higher indices, writes the new entry at index 0 and saturates the count at capacity (oldest entry dropped when full).

name: zw_screenshot_delete_handler
comment: Delete one entry from a fixed-capacity list (capacity +0x80, count +0x84): shifts the entries after the given index down by one slot and decrements the count.

name: printf_disabled_2
comment: Disabled printf variant 2: empty variadic stub (compiled-out diagnostic print).

name: FifoInit
comment: Initialise the global software FIFO: store buffer pointer and size and reset the read/write indices (descriptor at 0x2001DF94: +0 buffer, +4 size, +8 write index, +0xC read index). Returns 0, or -1 on null/zero arguments.

name: FifoDataLen
comment:
Return the number of bytes currently queued in the UART upgrade FIFO: write index (+8) minus
read index (+0xc) of the FIFO control block at 0x2001df94.

name: FifoRead
comment: Copy up to len bytes from the global software FIFO into buf, wrapping at the buffer end; returns the number of bytes actually copied (limited by available data).

name: FifoWrite
comment: Copy up to len bytes from buf into the global software FIFO, wrapping at the buffer end; returns the number of bytes actually stored (limited by free space).

name: zw_fifoInit
comment:
Reset the UART upgrade FIFO by zeroing the write index (+8) and read index (+0xc) of the
FIFO control block at 0x2001df94.

name: zw_draw_ParametrizedGlyph
comment:
Draws a run-length-encoded glyph/icon described by param_1 (x, y, data pointer, frame
count). The data starts with width/height, followed by (run_length, color) 16-bit pairs.
Colors with bit 0x20 are palette-indexed: bits 11+ select the palette bank (enabled via the
mask at param_1+6), otherwise the color is (color & 0x3ff)>>6; color 0xffdf means
transparent. Used for large icons and UI graphics.

name: zw_boot_logo
comment:
Draws the boot logo, an RLE-compressed indexed bitmap, at positionX/positionY.
Header: 16-bit width, 16-bit height, then (run_length, color) byte pairs; color 0x20 is
transparent. Wraps to the next row when the width boundary is reached.

name: zw_draw_element
comment:
Draws a 1bpp bitmap element described by p_Desc (x, y, bitmap pointer, fg, bg).
The bitmap starts with width and height bytes followed by MSB-first rows, 8 pixels per byte.
Set bits use the foreground color p_Desc[6], clear bits the background p_Desc[7]
(0x20 = transparent).

name: zw_drawGlyph2
comment:
Draws the set pixels of a 1bpp glyph (p_Desc: x, y, width, height, bitmap pointer,
foreground color). Rows are MSB-first, 8 pixels per byte; background pixels are skipped,
so the glyph is drawn transparently over existing content.

name: zw_draw_glyph_indexed
comment:
Draws an indexed 1bpp glyph described by param_1 (x, y, bitmap pointer, two colors).
Bitmap rows are MSB-first, 8 pixels per byte. Set pixels are drawn with param_1[6] when the
framebuffer pixel is 0, otherwise with param_1[7]; clear pixels are left untouched.

name: st7789_flush_framebuffer_indexed
comment: Push the whole 8bpp framebuffer to the LCD: sets the full-screen column/row window (320x240), issues RAMWR (0x2C) and streams every palette index converted to its 16-bit RGB565 palette entry over the bit-banged ST7789 interface.

name: zw_flush_framebuffer_rect
comment:
Blit an axis-aligned rectangle from the 8bpp indexed framebuffer to the ST7789 panel.
Params (x, y, width, height). Programs the panel address window with x..x+width / y..y+height,
issues RAMWR (0x2c), asserts CS, then for each row reads 320-byte-stride index bytes from the
framebuffer and writes the corresponding 16-bit palette entries, finally deasserts CS.
Used for partial-screen updates (popup areas, small panels) instead of a full flush.

name: zw_draw_hline_indexed
comment:
Draw a horizontal line of 'width' pixels into the 8bpp framebuffer at (positionX,
positionY) with the given palette index. Row stride is 320 bytes; no clipping is performed.

name: zw_draw_vline_indexed
comment: Draw a vertical line into the 8bpp framebuffer (320-byte stride at 0x2001dfa4), writing the given palette index for h pixels starting at (x,y).

name: zw_draw_line_horizontal_dashed
comment: Draw a dashed horizontal line into the 8bpp framebuffer using a 3-pixels-on / 1-pixel-off pattern.

name: zw_draw_line_vertical_dashed
comment:
Draw a vertical dashed line: steps down 'height' pixels in the 8bpp framebuffer (320-byte
stride), writing 3 pixels on and skipping every 4th (dash pattern), using the given palette index.

name: zw_draw_rect_filled_indexed
comment: Fill an axis-aligned rectangle in the 8bpp framebuffer with a palette index: loops rows y..y+h and writes w bytes per row at the 320-byte stride.

name: zw_draw_rect_indexed
comment:
Draws a rectangle outline (top, bottom, left and right edges; no fill) into the 8-bit
framebuffer at positionX/positionY with size width x height, using palette index
color & 0x7f.

name: zw_draw_dashed_rect_indexed
comment: Draws a dashed rectangle directly into the 8-bpp framebuffer (0x2001DFA4). Horizontal and vertical runs use a 5-on/1-off dash pattern (6-pixel period) and palette indices 2,6,3,4,7; width and height are in pixels. Used to frame cursor and frequency/period marker boxes.

name: zw_scope_ui_refresh
comment: Top-level oscilloscope UI refresh, called from main and the screenshot viewer. Clears or fades the framebuffer according to the persistence/decay settings, then draws the frame, saved waveform, traces/persistence, math trace, channel-level markers, trigger markers, measurement labels, FFT, frequency meter/counter, menus, math-roll panel, signal-generator window, cursor box and DMM setup.

name: zw_scope_draw_trace_xy_mode_hw_fb
comment:
XY-mode trace rendering.
Computes the sample count from the density settings+0x00, fetches the samples (or the
interpolated traces when settings[0xdf] is set), then plots palette index 5 for each sample
pair: CH1 sample -> x = sample+0x20 (clamped 0x3c..0x104), CH2 sample -> y = 0xf8-sample
(clamped 0x12..0xda).

name: zw_scope_redraw_frame
comment: Master scope frame redraw: clears the 320x240 framebuffer (76800 bytes) with the given colour and rebuilds the whole screen: XY plot UI, traces, channel/trigger indicators, menus, signal-generator window, trigger icons, temporary message box and the Shift/RTAuto status labels, then flushes the result to the panel.

name: zw_debug_dump
comment:
Debug dump of the sampled waveforms over the debug UART.
Returns early while the scope is running (settings[0xdc] set and no menu). Calls
zw_system_power_control(0), then either regenerates the interpolated traces and prints 300
samples of CH1 (and CH2 in dual mode) with wm_printf("%d "), or walks the capture in
blocks of 3000 samples (up to 60000) using zw_scope_fetch_samples_generic and prints them
the same way. Development-only signal inspection aid.

name: zw_IntToStr
comment:
Converts an unsigned integer (< 10000) to decimal ASCII without leading zeros and returns
the number of digits (1..4). Used by the UI for small numeric labels.

name: zw_draw_string_small
comment:
Draws a string with the small EN bitmap font (13 bytes per glyph, 13 rows tall, 8 pixels
wide; '.' is 4 pixels). Glyph bitmaps come from the fonts_small_EN table at (c-0x20)*0xd
and are written into the 8-bit framebuffer; backgroundColor 0x20 means transparent.
Returns the advanced X coordinate.

name: zw_draw_string_large
comment:
Draws a string with the large EN bitmap font (32 bytes per glyph, 16 rows tall, 10 pixels
wide; '.' is 4 pixels). Glyph bitmaps are fetched from the fonts_large_EN table at
(c-0x20)*0x20 and written into the 8-bit framebuffer; backgroundColor 0x20 means
transparent. Returns the advanced X coordinate.

name: zw_draw_string_large_integer
comment: Draw a large-font integer for the UI: accepts values below 10000 with at most 4 digits, converts them with IntToStr, renders them via draw_string_large and returns the advance width (10 pixels per digit, truncated to 8 bits).

name: zw_siggen_7-segment_digits
comment:
Draws one 7-segment-style digit for the signal-generator window.
Uses the large (19x27 px, 0x51 bytes/glyph) or small (10x14 px, 0x1c bytes/glyph) digit
bitmap font selected by param_6, at x=param_2, y=param_3, with foreground color param_4 and
background param_5 (0x20 = transparent).

name: zw_format_frequency_with_unit_str
comment:
Formats an unsigned 64-bit frequency (param_2 = low word, param_3 = high word) and stores
a 3-character unit string (' Hz', 'kHz', 'MHz' or 'GHz') in param_1. Thresholds are
1000 Hz, 1 MHz and 1 GHz; the scaled value is returned as a double via
__floatundidf/__divdf3.

name: zw_format_value_with_unit_generic_str
comment: Formats a signed 64-bit value into a compact 3-character engineering-notation string (e.g. 'Hz', 'mHz', 'uHz', 'kH'...) with a unit-class selector param_4 (1 = frequency/time, 3 = volts) and threshold-based rounding. Writes the suffix bytes to param_1; used by zw_scope_int_values for measurement labels.

name: zw_scope_int_values
comment: Formats and draws a numeric value with an engineering-unit suffix at pixel position (param_3, param_4). Selects the frequency-specific or generic formatter, applies decimal scaling from param_5, uses the large or small font (param_6) and returns the drawn width. Used by measurement labels, channel icons, cursor readouts and temporary messages.

name: zw_draw_CN
comment: Render one Chinese UI glyph: looks up the 0x18-byte glyph descriptor for the character and blits it with zw_drawGlyph2.

name: zw_dmm_chars_24x28
comment:
Draws one DMM small-font glyph at (param_2,param_3) with foreground param_4 and
background param_5 (0x20 = transparent), using the 24x28 digit font (0x54 bytes/glyph).
'.' is 8 px wide; '-'/'L'/'E'/'r'/'C' use dedicated bitmaps; glyph 0xff is blank.
Returns the next X coordinate (x + width + 2).

name: zw_dmm_chars_40x81
comment:
Draws one DMM large-font glyph at (param_2,param_3) with foreground param_4 and
background param_5 (0x20 = transparent), using the 40x81 digit font (0x195 bytes/glyph).
'.' is 0x14 px wide; '-'/'L'/'E'/'r'/'C' use dedicated bitmaps; 0xff is blank.
Returns the next X coordinate (x + width + 2).

name: zw_siggen_chars_32x53
comment: Render the signal-generator UI character set (32x53 pixel glyphs, 0xD4 bytes per glyph). The '.' is a special narrow glyph 0x12 pixels wide; returns the x coordinate after the glyph for continued drawing.

name: zw_scope_active_channel_icon-Math_label
comment:
Updates the active-channel indicator icon below the grid.
Tracks settings[0x11e] (0=CH1, 1=CH2, 2=Math) with a 30-frame redraw hold. Draws the
channel-switch icons in the active channel's color (0x3f for CH1, 0x5f for CH2), or clears
the area and draws the small 'Math' label in math mode.

name: zw_scope_icons_init
comment: Initializes the descriptor table for the persistent UI elements (channel-level markers and up/down/right arrows): fills x/y position, image pointer, palette index and masks. Called once from zw_ui_all_init; the descriptors are later moved by zw_scope_draw_channel_level and the menu renderer.

name: zw_ui_all_init
comment: Initialise the scope UI: three element/timer descriptors (timeouts 500/500/200000, element IDs 0x19/0xD9/0x87), build the CH2 colour gradient for the selected palette mode (settings[0x112]), initialise the status icons and clear the framebuffer.

name: zw_scope_memory_bar
comment: Draws the acquisition-memory bar above the graticule: converts the visible window and total capture depth through zw_calculate_float_div_and_scale and the time/div settings, clamps the segment to the 0x60-px bar starting at x=0x70 and renders the highlighted window. Called from zw_scope_fullscreen and the XY-mode UI.

name: zw_scope_grid
comment: Draws the scope graticule into the 8-bpp framebuffer as a dotted grid with 25-pixel spacing (5-pixel dot pitch), choosing dotted/dashed style from settings[0x111] and handling the split-screen and zoom layouts from settings[0x10C]/[0x135]. Called by zw_scope_fullscreen.

name: zw_scope_draw_zoom_window_overlay_hw_fb
comment:
Draws the zoom-window overlay: computes the zoomed window start/end columns from the saved
zoom time base (settings[0x134]) and the roll offset settings+0x138/+0x13c, then fills the
two regions outside the window (rows 0x12..0x82) to dim the non-zoomed part of the trace.

name: zw_scope_draw_zoom_window_borders_hw_fb
comment: Draw the 2-pixel-wide zoom-window borders around the current zoom positions: vertical separator lines using palette colours 10 and 0x0C on the framebuffer.

name: zw_scope_draw_channel_level
comment: Positions the CH1/CH2 channel-level markers (edge arrows) from the vertical offsets in settings +0x48/+0x88, taking the zoom/split-screen mode settings[0x135] into account and clamping the markers to the plot area. Called from zw_scope_ui_refresh.

name: zw_scope_draw_trigger_level_ui
comment:
Draws the trigger-level indicator line, with a 20-frame fade-out timer kept in a global.
Maps the trigger level settings+0x40 (ADC units) to a screen row, clamps it to the display
area, selects palette 0x3f/0x5f based on settings[0x38], stores the row in the trigger UI
element and draws the line plus the trigger element.

name: zw_scope_draw_horizontal_trigger_icon
comment:
Draws the horizontal trigger-position icon at the top of the waveform grid.
Converts the trigger time offset (settings+0x1c minus +0x24, scaled by 25) into grid
columns using the sample rate settings+0x14, then places the 'T' icon at the left edge
(10), the right edge (0x136-width) or an arrow at the offset position (0xa0 + offset -
width/2). Skipped in XY mode.

name: zw_scope_icons-channel_modes
comment: Draws the CH1/CH2 status icons for the normal and XY fullscreen views: channel-enable colors, V/div reading via zw_scope_int_values, AC/DC coupling icon, 1X/10X/100X probe text and the CH2 block when dual-channel mode is active. Called from zw_scope_fullscreen and zw_scope_XY_mode_fullscreen_ui.

name: zw_scope_fullscreen
comment: Full-screen scope overlay: when the zoom-window enable flag (settings offset 0x135) is set draws the zoom overlay and borders, then the graticule/grid, channel and trigger icons, the math label, the memory-usage bar and the battery icon.

name: zw_scope_draw_xy_mode_indicators_hw_fb
comment:
Draws the XY-mode position indicators: places the right-arrow element from the CH1
vertical offset settings+0x88 and the down-arrow element from the CH2 offset settings+0x48,
clamping both to the display area, then draws them.

name: zw_scope_XY_grid
comment:
Draws the XY-mode grid.
settings[0x10c] enables the grid and settings[0x111] selects the style (0=dots, 1=dashed,
2=solid), mapping to palette indices 0/10/11/12. Grid lines are drawn every 5 or 25
pixels into the primary and overlay framebuffers (two 320x240 views at different bases).

name: zw_scope_XY_mode_fullscreen_ui
comment:
Draw the full-screen UI for X-Y mode: XY grid (style 0xb), channel-mode icons, the
Math label when a math channel is enabled (settings[2]), the memory/sample bar, and the
battery indicator with fill overlay.

name: zw_draw_battery_ui_hw_fb
comment:
Draw the battery indicator: renders the battery UI element (icon frame) then the fill-level
overlay via zw_draw_battery_icon_overlay.

name: zw_scope_menu_cn_init
comment:
Initializes the Chinese scope-menu UI element table: the menu background bitmap at
(250,41), the measurements/trigger/display/settings icons at their screen positions, and
the up/left arrow indicators, setting each element's colors and clearing the associated
state globals.

name: zw_scope_ch1_measurements_menu
comment:
CH1 measurements menu.
Maintains selection index DAT_0802a140 over 15 rows. Key 4/3 move down/up within a column;
keys 0x13/0xb move between the two columns (4 rows apart, wrapping between rows 3 and
0xb). Key 2 toggles the measurement-enable bit (1<<index) in the mask settings+0x6c; row
0xe is a select-all/clear-all row that saves the old mask and sets 0x7fff.

name: zw_scope_calibration_menu_handler
comment: Handles the manual calibration menu: moves a 15-entry selection, toggles individual calibration bits in settings +0xAC (entry 14 temporarily forces 0x7FFF), and shows the corresponding popups. Called from zw_scope_menu_dispatch_logic.

name: zw_scope_trigger_menu_handler_ui
comment:
Trigger-menu key handler.
Maintains the selected row DAT_0802a308 in 0..7: keys 4/3 move down/up by one, 0x13/0xb by two,
with wraparound at 8. Key 2 invokes the row action through the jump table at 0x08061f98
(Ghidra could not recover the table: 'too many branches').

name: zw_scope_display_menu_handler_ui
comment: Key handler for the Display settings page: moves the 8-entry selection, toggles F-meter/Counter enables, applies CH1/CH2 20 MHz bandwidth limiting via zw_scope_set_bandwidth_limit, adjusts LCD backlight PWM (zw_lcd_set_pwm), and redraws the page. Called from zw_scope_menu_dispatch_logic.

name: zw_scope_menu_state_machine
comment: System-settings menu state machine (menu page 3). Navigates the 9-entry settings list and executes the selected action: version popup ('v3.0.7_III'), display settings, hardware check, FPGA firmware upgrade over UART3 (zw_firmware_uart_upgrade), LCD re-init/backlight control, and power off/on sequencing. Called from zw_scope_menu_dispatch_logic.

name: zw_scope_menu_dispatch_logic
comment:
Top-level key dispatcher for the scope menus.
Key 6 toggles the menu/measurement bit in settings[0x121] (scope mode only) and returns
0xff when consumed. Otherwise, while a menu is active, keys 0x0a/0x12/0x08/0x10/0x18 select
menu page 0..4 (stored in DAT_0802adfc) and call the matching handler: 0 = CH1
measurements menu, 1 = calibration menu UI, 2 = trigger menu UI, 3 = display menu UI,
4 = menu state machine.

name: zw_scope_menu_Meas
comment: Draws the Measurements menu page: twelve measurement slots in a 4x3 grid (frequency, period, Vpp, Vavg, Vrms, duty cycle, pulse width, rise/fall time, etc.). param_1 selects CH1 (0) or CH2; enabled slots are highlighted with palette 0x3F/0x5F according to the bitmask at settings +0x6C (CH1) / +0xAC (CH2). Called from zw_scope_menu.

name: zw_scope_menu_Trig
comment: Draws the Trigger menu page: trigger mode, slope, source (CH1/CH2), coupling and auto/normal options are highlighted according to settings +0x38..+0x3B and +0xE8. Called from zw_scope_menu.

name: zw_scope_menu_Disp
comment: Draws the Display settings menu page: F-meter and Counter ON/OFF, CH1 and CH2 20 MHz bandwidth-limit ON/OFF, and the related display options, highlighting the current selections from settings +0x116/+0x141/+0x144/+0x145. Rendered by the scope menu (zw_scope_menu).

name: zw_scope_menu_Set
comment: Draws the Settings menu page: the icon/title bar, the CN/EN language indicator, selection markers for the available settings entries and the highlighted item driven by settings +0xF9/+0xFB/+0xFC/+0x110. Called from zw_scope_menu.

name: zw_scope_menu
comment:
Draws the scope menu bar.
While settings[0x121] bit 0 is set, selects the Chinese or English menu bitmap
(settings[0xe8]), draws the background rectangle (x-1, y-1, 0x45 x 200, color 0xd), the
menu element, and the highlighted row element at y+0x10+index*0x28. Then dispatches to the
per-menu drawing routine via the jump table at 0x08062034 (not recovered by Ghidra).

name: zw_scope_restore_measurements_bits_logic
comment:
Restore the CH1 measurements enable bitmask after leaving the measurement page.
If the backup-active flag at 0x2000a1a8 is set, copies the saved mask at 0x2000a1c4 back into
settings+0x6c (bit-per-measurement enables). The CH1 menu's key 0x0e toggles a 'show all'
(0x7fff) mode and stores/restores this backup.

name: zw_scope_quick_action_handler
comment: Quick-action key handler for the normal scope view (settings[1]==1): CH1/CH2 on/off (event 0x56), AC/DC coupling (event 8), probe attenuation 1X/10X/100X (event 0x10), trigger mode/slope/source and cursor selection, updating settings and showing short status popups. Called from main.

name: zw_draw_popup_message
comment:
Show a temporary on-screen text popup.
Sets the popup-active flag (0x2000a260), arms the popup timer (0x2000a254) for time_ms*1000 us,
then fills the shared popup descriptor (0x2000a1e4): length at +0, up to 100 text bytes at +2,
centered x at +0x66 (160 - 5*len for even len, 155 - 10*(len>>1) for odd len), y=110 at +0x68,
foreground color at +0x6a and background at +0x6c. The text is byte-copied (not NUL terminated)
from the caller's string. Rendering is done by zw_ui_render_temporary_message_ui until the timer
expires. Used throughout the UI/HAL for status and error messages.

name: zw_ui_show_temporary_message_logic
comment:
Show a temporary popup carrying six integer values instead of text.
Sets popup-active (0x2000a260), arms the popup timer (0x2000a254) for param_7*1000 us, clears the
descriptor length (0x2000a1e4)=0 and stores param_1..param_6 as six dwords at +0..+0x14 of the same
descriptor. A zero length tells zw_ui_render_temporary_message_ui to call zw_scope_int_values with
these six values, which formats/draws them in the popup area (message length 0 => value mode).

name: zw_ui_render_temporary_message_ui
comment:
Render/expire the shared temporary popup (called from the UI loop).
If popup-active is clear it does nothing. If the popup timer expired it clears the active flag.
Otherwise, zero length => zw_scope_int_values(6 stored dwords); non-zero length => zw_draw_string_large
of the stored text with stored x/y and fg/bg colors. The display is flushed by the caller.

name: zw_math_roll_menu_handler
comment: Key handler for the Math/Roll menu overlay (settings[0x121] bit 5): event 0x86 opens/closes the panel, event 0x94 toggles the roll mode, up/down selects the math operation and OK commits settings[0x148]/[0x149]. Called from main; returns 0xFF when the event is consumed.

name: zw_scope_menu_math-roll
comment: Draws the Math/Roll overlay panel when settings[0x121] bit 5 is set: framed popup with highlight boxes for the math operation (settings[0x148] 1/2) and roll enable (settings[0x149]) plus the math/roll menu icons. Called from zw_scope_ui_refresh and zw_scope_redraw_frame.

name: zw_gpio_init_hw
comment:
Configure GPIO pin(s): enables the GPIO clock (0x40000E00 |= 0x800), maps the custom mode
argument to the HAL init structure (1 -> Mode=2/output, 0 -> Mode=1/input, otherwise copied),
maps the pull argument (0 -> 0x13, 1 -> 0x14, other -> 0x12), fills Pin=mask and calls
HAL_GPIO_Init. Used everywhere a pin changes direction or pull.

name: zw_set_bits
comment: Atomically-ish set bits: *word |= mask. Used for peripheral register bit manipulation.

name: zw_clear_bits
comment: Clear bits: *word &= ~mask. Used for peripheral register bit manipulation.

name: zw_pwm_init
comment:
Initializes the three PWM handles on the PWM block at 0x40011E00: hpwm0 at 0x20030BE0,
hpwm1 at 0x20030C0C and the LCD-backlight channel at 0x20030BB4, each with its prescaler,
period and channel settings. Starts hpwm0, starts then immediately stops hpwm1, and leaves
the backlight channel initialized but stopped until zw_lcd_set_pwm starts it.

name: zw_pwm_set_duty_cycle_hw
comment:
Set a PWM duty cycle on whichever channel is requested.
param_1 = channel, param_2 (r1) = pulse/duty value. Finds the owner of the channel by comparing
hpwm0->Channel and hpwm1->Channel (+0x28); if neither matches, the backlight PWM handle is used.
Calls HAL_PWM_Duty_Set(handle, channel, pulse).

name: HAL_PWM_Start_wrapper
comment:
HAL wrapper used by battery/charge code: HAL_PWM_Start on the handle whose Channel field
(+0x28) matches param_1; hpwm0 and hpwm1 are checked, otherwise the backlight PWM handle is used.

name: HAL_PWM_Stop_wrapper
comment:
HAL wrapper used by battery/charge code: HAL_PWM_Stop on the handle whose Channel field
(+0x28) matches param_1; hpwm0 and hpwm1 are checked, otherwise the backlight PWM handle is used.

name: zw_lcd_set_pwm
comment:
LCD backlight brightness control: if the requested duty is non-zero, programs the
backlight PWM channel (hpwm_backlight) with zw_pwm_set_duty_cycle_hw and starts it via
HAL_PWM_Start_wrapper; duty 0 stops the channel.

name: zw_pwm_control_hw
comment:
Auxiliary PWM control (hpwm0, used for the DMM bias/charge supply): non-zero duty programs
the channel and starts it via HAL_PWM_Start_wrapper; duty 0 stops it.

name: zw_HAL_PWM_Start_wrapper
comment:
Start hpwm1, the system power/boost converter PWM. Called by zw_system_power_control:
passes hpwm1's channel field (handle+0x28) to HAL_PWM_Start_wrapper, which resolves it back to
the hpwm1 handle and enables the channel.

name: zw_HAL_PWM_Stop_wrapper
comment:
Stop hpwm1, the system power/boost converter PWM. Called by zw_system_power_control:
passes hpwm1's channel field (handle+0x28) to HAL_PWM_Stop_wrapper, which resolves it back to
the hpwm1 handle and disables the channel.

name: zw_fpga_spi_write_buf
comment: Transmit one bootloader data frame on UART3: length field (len-1 as one byte for len<=0x100, otherwise two bytes), payload, then XOR checksum over the length and payload bytes. Called with data=NULL to emit a bare length header for read requests.

name: zw_gpio_init_uart_pins_hw_setup
comment: Configure the extra GPIOA lines used by the UART firmware-upgrade path: PA15 (mask 0x8000) as input and PA11 (mask 0x800) as output via zw_gpio_init_hw.

name: zw_uart_init_with_fifo_hw_setup
comment: Configure UART3 for the FPGA bridge bootloader (pins/baud and RX interrupt) and initialise the software FIFO descriptor at 0x2001DF94 with buffer 0x2001BB30.

name: zw_uart_rx_interrupt_handler_logic
comment: Shared UART IRQ logic for UART1's interrupt: services the UART3 FPGA link (push RX bytes into the software FIFO and kick the bootloader watchdog), UART4 DMM frames and the voice-control UART. Called from UART1_IRQHandler.

name: zw_fpga_spi_cmd_done
comment: Wait for the 'y' (0x79) ACK from the FPGA bridge bootloader on UART3. Polls huart3_fpga for a received byte, retrying for roughly the requested number of iterations, and returns non-zero when the ACK is seen, 0 on timeout. Used after bootloader commands and data packets.

name: zw_uart_sync_and_handshake_bootloader
comment: Send the 0x7F sync byte on UART3 and wait for the 'y' reply so the bridge MCU enters its command bootloader. Returns non-zero on success. This link is UART3 (huart3_fpga), not SPI.

name: zw_fpga_spi_cmd_wait
comment: Send a one-byte bootloader command on UART3 followed by its bitwise complement, then wait for the 'y' ACK (up to 500 retries with delays). Used for command-only operations such as read/write/erase; returns non-zero on success.

name: zw_fpga_spi_set_addr
comment: Program the bootloader flash address: command 0x21, a 4-byte address and an XOR checksum, then wait for the ACK. Subsequent read, write and erase commands act on this address.

name: zw_uart_send_data_packet_bootloader
comment: Send the 0x44 data-packet command to the bootloader, stream the length/payload/checksum frame via zw_fpga_spi_write_buf, and wait for the 'y' ACK. Returns non-zero on success.

name: zw_fpga_spi_set_flash_addr_safe_hw
comment: Send command 0x21 to the FPGA bootloader and, on success, program the flash address pointer via zw_fpga_spi_set_addr. Safe wrapper used before a page access.

name: zw_fpga_spi_write_packet_and_wait_hw
comment: Send bootloader command 0x44 (data packet), transmit one length/payload/checksum packet and wait for the completion ACK; the wait timeout scales with packet length. Returns non-zero on success.

name: zw_fpga_write_flash_page
comment: Write up to one block at a flash address through the bootloader: command 0x31 for <=0x100 bytes or 0x33 for larger blocks, program the address, optionally issue command 0 depending on a flash-config byte, stream the payload with zw_fpga_spi_write_buf and wait for the ACK (timeout scales with length).

name: zw_fpga_spi_read_flash_page_hw
comment: Read a block from bootloader flash: command 0x11 for <=0x100 bytes or 0x13 for larger, program the address, send a bare length header, wait for the ACK, then collect the returned bytes from the software RX FIFO into the caller buffer.

name: zw_fpga_spi_send_magic_A2_hw
comment: Send magic command 0xA2 (command byte plus complement) to the FPGA bridge bootloader and wait for the 'y' ACK. Part of the upgrade-entry handshake.

name: zw_fpga_spi_send_magic_A3_hw
comment: Send magic command 0xA3 (command byte plus complement) to the FPGA bridge bootloader and wait for the 'y' ACK. Used as the special erase/mode command, including the MCU cor2 image path.

name: zw_fpga_flash_erase
comment: Erase a flash range through the FPGA bridge bootloader. Rounds the range to 4 KB pages and sends a page list (page number = addr>>12, with bit 15 set on 32 KB-boundary markers) in packets of up to 255 entries via command 0x44. If addr < 0x80 (cor2 MCU image at offset 0) it instead issues magic command 0xA3. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

name: zw_fpga_verify_data_block
comment: Verify an uploaded block by reading it back through the bootloader and comparing it against the source buffer; aborts on mismatch. Called at the end of each firmware blob upload.

name: zw_fpga_firmware_upload_setup
comment: Stream a firmware blob to the bootloader in chunks of config_byte*0x100 bytes using zw_fpga_write_flash_page, then verify the written range with zw_fpga_verify_data_block. Stops early when a page write fails.

name: zw_fpga_write_boot_header_hw_setup
comment: Write the FPGA boot header at the start of config flash through the bootloader: first half-word 0x5AA5 magic followed by size/checksum header fields describing the payload.

name: zw_fpga_read_config_reg_hw_read
comment: Read an FPGA configuration register remotely through the bootloader link. Selects one of the bridge-side addresses 0x4000100C/0x40001010/0x40001014/0x4000102C/0x40001030, using the initial key value 0x8001045A, and returns the 32-bit result.

name: zw_uart_bootloader_init_hw_setup
comment: Probe and initialise the FPGA bridge bootloader over UART3: force 115200 baud when the config byte is < 0x20, sync handshake, read the bootloader version string and set FPGA revision flags from its characters, then check byte 0 of config flash and upload fpga_firmware_0 (0x14F8 bytes) when missing/old, re-entering recursively. Called after the UART3/FIFO hardware setup.

name: zw_fpga_reset_pulse_hw_ctl
comment: Pulse the FPGA bridge reset line (PA11): drive low, delay, then release high. Used to restart the bridge MCU into its bootloader/flash during upgrade.

name: zw_uart_upgrade_prepare_hw_setup
comment: Prepare the hardware path for UART firmware upgrade: configures the upgrade GPIO pins, initialises the UART with FIFO settings, drives the PA15 control line, pulses the FPGA reset and waits 2 seconds before re-initialising the UART for the ROM bootloader protocol.

name: zw_system_deinit_early
comment: Early system de-init around an FPGA/MCU firmware upgrade: tear down interrupt/peripheral state and quiesce the acquisition path before the bootloader takes over the link.

name: zw_fpga_flash_write_at_zero_hw_util
comment: Write a firmware block at bootloader flash offset 0: set the address with zw_fpga_spi_set_flash_addr_safe_hw(0) and stream the data through zw_fpga_write_flash_page. Used for the cor2 MCU image loaded at 0x08000000.

name: zw_fpga_init_upgrade_sequence_logic
comment: Entry point of an FPGA/MCU upgrade: initialise the UART3 bootloader link, run the sync/magic handshake and erase the target flash before uploading images.

name: zw_fpga_firmware_upload
comment: Full FPGA/MCU firmware upgrade. Erases the config-flash window at 0x7FFF6000 (length 0xA000) and uploads fpga_firmware_1 (0xAA0 bytes), then selects by detected FPGA version: fpga_firmware_2_v1 (0x6100), fpga_firmware_3 (0x62D0) or fpga_firmware_2_v2 (0x6100) at 0x7FFF6B00. Finally erases the 0x0-0x8000 window and uploads mcu_cor2_firmware (0x3788 bytes) at offset 0.

name: zw_firmware_uart_upgrade
SystemInit
comment: Clears VIC active/pending interrupt state.

name: trap_c
comment: Prints the exception register frame and halts.

name: board_init
comment: VIC init plus UART0 console configuration.

name: _out_uart
comment:
mpaland printf output hook for the debug UART (UART0).
Spins until the UART0 transmit FIFO has room (status register +0x1c low 6 bits <= 0x1f), then writes
the character to the data register (+0x20). Installed as _putchar's uart output routine.

name: _out_null
comment:
mpaland printf output hook that silently discards a character (null output); used when the
printf backend is a no-op. Single return, no side effects.

name: _out_rev
_ntoa_format
comment:
printf integer helper: finishes a converted number by zero-padding to the requested
precision, appending an optional decimal point/digit, adding sign or base prefix (0x, 0b)
and width padding, then emitting the digits through _out_rev.

name: _ntoa_long
comment:
printf helper: converts an unsigned long to ASCII in base 10/16/8/2 (upper or lower
case) by repeated division, then calls _ntoa_format for padding and prefixes.

name: _ntoa_long_long
comment:
printf helper: converts an unsigned 64-bit value to ASCII using __udivdi3/__umoddi3 for
base 10/16/8/2, then calls _ntoa_format for padding and prefixes.

name: _ftoa
comment:
printf %f conversion: splits the double into integer and fraction parts, rounds to the
requested precision, emits the integer digits and fractional digits through _out_rev, and
falls back to _etoa for very large magnitudes. Uses the soft-float helpers.

name: _etoa
comment:
printf %e/%g conversion: normalizes the double to d.ddd * 10^exp, rounds the mantissa
digits and emits the exponent (sign + zero-padded digits) using _ntoa_long._out_rev.

name: _vsnprintf
comment:
Core of the firmware printf implementation (mpaland-style _vsnprintf).
Parses flags, width, precision and length modifiers from the format string and dispatches
to _ntoa_long, _ntoa_long_long, _ftoa, _etoa and _out_rev. Backs printf/sprintf and the
debug/log output routines.

name: fputc
comment:
fputc for the newlib stdio backend: bypasses the FILE machinery and writes the character
directly to the debug UART0, spinning while the TX FIFO is full (status +0x1c low 6 bits).
Returns 0 unconditionally.

name: wm_printf
comment: wm_printf: W806 printf backend. Formats into a local buffer with _vsnprintf (unlimited length) and writes the result through the _out_uart character sink.

name: vTaskSwitchContext
comment: FreeRTOS vTaskSwitchContext: if the scheduler is suspended sets xYieldPending and returns; otherwise clears xYieldPending, scans uxTopReadyPriority downward through pxReadyTasksLists advancing the list cursor and sets pxCurrentTCB. Calls wm_printf assertions if no ready task is found.
